utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: Okay, um, I think maybe we can start? Is everyone here, or are we waiting on-

utterances.speaker: Kofi
utterances.text: Wei's still getting his laptop sorted, I saw him in the corridor.

utterances.speaker: Wei
utterances.text: Here. Go.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: Great. So, uh, thanks for coming in on a Thursday, I know the first week back is always, you know, messy.

utterances.speaker: Yuki
utterances.text: Messy is generous. My inbox has like four hundred things from the break.

utterances.speaker: Kofi
utterances.text: Four hundred, that's nothing, I had Sione forward me his whole-

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: Sorry, Kofi, can we, I think maybe we should do the budget thing first and then catch up on inboxes?

utterances.speaker: Kofi
utterances.text: Yeah, yeah, fair.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: So the, um, the cut. Next year's number came down from the leadership group before the holidays, and it's eight percent.

utterances.speaker: Yuki
utterances.text: Eight percent of what, the whole company spend or just the controllable bits?

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: I think, um, maybe the whole operating budget? I'd have to check the memo.

utterances.speaker: Wei
utterances.text: Check it.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: I will. I will, after this. Anyway, the question is how we apply it, and, uh, nothing's fixed yet.

utterances.speaker: Yuki
utterances.text: Right, because the big picture is we need to land somewhere sensible and not wreck anyone's year.

utterances.speaker: Kofi
utterances.text: Which is basically impossible if you-

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: Kofi, let people finish, please.

utterances.speaker: Kofi
utterances.text: Sorry, go on.

utterances.speaker: Yuki
utterances.text: No, I was done. I just meant it's a lot of moving parts.

utterances.speaker: Ivan
utterances.text: Can I, um. Can I say something?

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: Of course, Ivan, please.

utterances.speaker: Ivan
utterances.text: So, what if we just, um, take eight percent off every department. Same cut for all of them.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: Across the board, you mean?

utterances.speaker: Ivan
utterances.text: Yeah. Across the board. Every department's line, down eight.

utterances.speaker: Wei
utterances.text: Flat cut.

utterances.speaker: Ivan
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: Okay, I think maybe that's, um, worth hearing out. Ivan, what's the thinking?

utterances.speaker: Ivan
utterances.text: Well, it's easy to explain, for one. Nobody has to defend a number against anybody else's.

utterances.speaker: Kofi
utterances.text: People will still complain though, they always-

utterances.speaker: Ivan
utterances.text: They will, but nobody can say they got singled out. That's the, the thing people care about.

utterances.speaker: Yuki
utterances.text: That's a fair point, honestly. Perception matters a lot in these rounds.

utterances.speaker: Ivan
utterances.text: And the timing works. The budget file locks around the twentieth, and a flat percentage is something we can just load in. No back and forth with fifteen heads.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: Mm.

utterances.speaker: Ivan
utterances.text: Plus, um, once they have the new total, each head can decide where it comes out of. Hiring, travel, whatever they'd rather give up.

utterances.speaker: Wei
utterances.text: So we don't pick for them.

utterances.speaker: Ivan
utterances.text: Right. They know their own areas better than we do.

utterances.speaker: Kofi
utterances.text: Except that some of them will just, like, cut the training line and leave the same headcount, and then we-

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: Kofi, hang on, I think maybe let's park that. Ivan hasn't finished, has he?

utterances.speaker: Ivan
utterances.text: No, that was mostly it. Sorry, I'm not great at this.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: No, no, that was clear. Really clear.

utterances.speaker: Yuki
utterances.text: I do wonder if some departments are already lean, though. Like, eight percent on a department that's mostly salaries is a different animal.

utterances.speaker: Wei
utterances.text: True.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: Yeah. Um. That's a, a good flag, Yuki, I think maybe we need numbers for that.

utterances.speaker: Yuki
utterances.text: I mean, I don't have them. I just have a feeling about it.

utterances.speaker: Kofi
utterances.text: Facilities is basically all fixed cost. Rent and, you know, the contract with-

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: Esra's team handles the facilities contract, right?

utterances.speaker: Kofi
utterances.text: Yeah, Esra, and Laszlo sits on that too, I think.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: Okay. We might want to ask Esra what's actually flexible there.

utterances.speaker: Wei
utterances.text: Ask her.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: I'll, uh, I'll send something this afternoon. Or tomorrow. Tomorrow's probably better.

utterances.speaker: Yuki
utterances.text: Is anyone else getting a weird error when they open the shared forecast sheet? It keeps greying out the columns.

utterances.speaker: Ivan
utterances.text: Mine did that yesterday.

utterances.speaker: Kofi
utterances.text: It's because someone has it open in the old version. Gabor, I think. He never closes anything.

utterances.speaker: Wei
utterances.text: Tell him.

utterances.speaker: Kofi
utterances.text: I did, twice.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: Okay, okay, I think maybe that's a thing for IT. Can someone just message them?

utterances.speaker: Yuki
utterances.text: I'll do it, it's like two lines.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: Thanks, Yuki.

utterances.speaker: Kofi
utterances.text: Speaking of Gabor, did you see he's moving to the Rotterdam office in March?

utterances.speaker: Yuki
utterances.text: No way. Really? I thought that fell through.

utterances.speaker: Kofi
utterances.text: Camille told me. Apparently they sorted the visa thing.

utterances.speaker: Ivan
utterances.text: He talked about Rotterdam before. His partner's from there.

utterances.speaker: Yuki
utterances.text: Oh, that makes sense then. Good for him.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: Um, that's lovely. I think maybe we should, though, go back to the, the cut.

utterances.speaker: Kofi
utterances.text: Sorry, yeah. Tangent.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: No, it's fine, it's, um, it's a Thursday. But we do have to actually get somewhere.

utterances.speaker: Wei
utterances.text: Where's the deadline from?

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: Ivan said the twentieth, and I think that's right, I'd want to confirm with Beatriz.

utterances.speaker: Wei
utterances.text: Beatriz owns the file.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: She does. She owns the file lock.

utterances.speaker: Yuki
utterances.text: And is the twentieth hard or is it like, a soft-ish date?

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: I think it's soft-ish? Honestly I don't know.

utterances.speaker: Kofi
utterances.text: Last year they let it slide a week, but then the quarter close got-

utterances.speaker: Yuki
utterances.text: Right, and everyone was cranky.

utterances.speaker: Ivan
utterances.text: I thought it didn't slide last year. I thought it was the, um, the twenty-fourth that was the real one.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: Could be. I'd have to look back.

utterances.speaker: Wei
utterances.text: Not important now.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: No. No, you're right.

utterances.speaker: Yuki
utterances.text: What I keep coming back to is whether finance leadership cares more about speed or fairness here. Like, which one do they actually want.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: Um, I think maybe both, which is the annoying answer.

utterances.speaker: Kofi
utterances.text: They always want both.

utterances.speaker: Yuki
utterances.text: Mm. Fair.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: Okay. So where are we? We have, um, the flat cut on the table. Does anyone want to, uh, say something about that?

utterances.speaker: Wei
utterances.text: Not yet.

utterances.speaker: Kofi
utterances.text: I'd want to see what it does in dollars by department before I say anything. Like, a real table, not a percentage.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: That seems reasonable. Could you, Kofi, pull that together? Or, uh, maybe Ivan, since it was your idea-

utterances.speaker: Ivan
utterances.text: I can try. Which sheet has last year's actuals?

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: It's in the, um, the shared drive, under planning, I think? Or maybe it's under the archive folder.

utterances.speaker: Kofi
utterances.text: Planning. The archive one is two years back.

utterances.speaker: Ivan
utterances.text: Okay. I'll find it.

utterances.speaker: Yuki
utterances.text: Should we loop in the department heads before we get too far? Or is that jumping ahead?

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: I think maybe it's early. I don't want to send out a number that we haven't, you know, agreed on.

utterances.speaker: Yuki
utterances.text: Sure, yeah. I just don't want them blindsided.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: No, of course. We'll tell them well before the twentieth.

utterances.speaker: Wei
utterances.text: How much before.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: Um. Probably a week? Ish?

utterances.speaker: Wei
utterances.text: Ish.

utterances.speaker: Kofi
utterances.text: A week isn't enough for the bigger departments, they need to run it by their own people and-

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: Okay, that's, that's another thing to think about. Let's write it down.

utterances.speaker: Yuki
utterances.text: I'll put it in the notes.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: Thank you. Right. So, I have a hard stop in about five minutes, there's a thing with Beatriz about the audit calendar.

utterances.speaker: Kofi
utterances.text: Is that the one about the sampling dates?

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: Yes, that one, it keeps moving.

utterances.speaker: Kofi
utterances.text: Of course it does.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: So, um, next steps. Ivan, the table by department. I'll check the memo on what the eight percent applies to, and ask Esra about facilities.

utterances.speaker: Yuki
utterances.text: And I'll ping IT about the sheet.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: Great. And we'll come back to this next time, I think, once we have the numbers in front of us.

utterances.speaker: Wei
utterances.text: Fine.

utterances.speaker: Ivan
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: Okay. Thanks everyone. I'm going to run, sorry, I'm late already.

utterances.speaker: Kofi
utterances.text: Go, go. We'll sort out the notes.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: Okay, um, I think maybe we can start. Is, uh, is everybody-

utterances.speaker: Kofi
utterances.text: Ivan's here, Yuki's here, Wei's here. We're all here.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: Great. Thanks. So, I looked at the memo, finally.

utterances.speaker: Wei
utterances.text: And?

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: Whole operating budget. Not just the controllable bits. So, um, Yuki, that answers your question from last week.

utterances.speaker: Yuki
utterances.text: Okay, good. Bigger than I'd hoped, but good to know.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: And I, uh, I did write to Esra about facilities. She hasn't come back yet.

utterances.speaker: Kofi
utterances.text: She never replies before Wednesday. Ask Laszlo, he'll know.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: I think maybe I'll give her till Friday first.

utterances.speaker: Ivan
utterances.text: I did the, um, the table. By department. It's in the folder.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: Oh, wonderful. Thank you, Ivan. Did you find the actuals okay?

utterances.speaker: Ivan
utterances.text: Planning folder, like you said. Kofi was right about the archive one.

utterances.speaker: Kofi
utterances.text: Told you.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: So, uh, has everyone seen it? Or, I mean, opened it?

utterances.speaker: Yuki
utterances.text: I skimmed it on the train. Sorry, big picture only.

utterances.speaker: Kofi
utterances.text: I read it. The flat one hits sales ops weirdly hard, their number is mostly salaries so-

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: Kofi, can we, I think maybe let Wei go first? He said he had something.

utterances.speaker: Wei
utterances.text: Yeah. I went through the contract register.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: Oh, right, the, um, the commitments thing.

utterances.speaker: Wei
utterances.text: Sixty-two percent of the budget is already tied up in multi-year contracts. Can't touch it this cycle.

utterances.speaker: Ivan
utterances.text: Sixty-two? I thought it was around half.

utterances.speaker: Wei
utterances.text: It's sixty-two. I counted twice.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: Okay, so, um, what does that mean for the cut, practically?

utterances.speaker: Wei
utterances.text: Eight percent of the whole thing comes out of what's left. Roughly a fifth of the uncommitted lines. Twenty-one, about.

utterances.speaker: Kofi
utterances.text: Hang on, that's, that's a lot more than eight-

utterances.speaker: Wei
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: Huh. Okay. Um. That changes the feel of it, doesn't it.

utterances.speaker: Ivan
utterances.text: So the flat one isn't really flat then. Not in what people feel.

utterances.speaker: Wei
utterances.text: Flat on paper.

utterances.speaker: Yuki
utterances.text: Right, and, so, I mean, if it's a fifth of what's actually movable, then, um, why are we spreading it over everything?

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: Say more?

utterances.speaker: Yuki
utterances.text: What if we aim it? Travel, contractors, events. The uncommitted stuff in those. Take the eight out of there and leave the rest.

utterances.speaker: Kofi
utterances.text: Same total?

utterances.speaker: Yuki
utterances.text: Same total, yeah. Same eight percent, it just lands somewhere specific.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: So, um, targeted, you mean. Instead of everyone.

utterances.speaker: Yuki
utterances.text: Yes. Targeted.

utterances.speaker: Wei
utterances.text: Which lines exactly.

utterances.speaker: Yuki
utterances.text: I'd need the sheet for exact. Those three are the obvious ones, there's more flexibility there.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: Mm. Okay.

utterances.speaker: Ivan
utterances.text: Is there enough in those three to cover it? Like, in dollars?

utterances.speaker: Yuki
utterances.text: I haven't, I haven't run that. I think so? Kofi, you've got the travel numbers.

utterances.speaker: Kofi
utterances.text: Somewhere. I'd have to dig.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: That's something we'd want to check, I think maybe.

utterances.speaker: Yuki
utterances.text: The reason I like it, though, is the other way squeezes everything evenly. If every uncommitted line loses a fifth, that includes the tooling renewals.

utterances.speaker: Ivan
utterances.text: The product ones?

utterances.speaker: Yuki
utterances.text: Yeah, those come due in the second quarter. Spread thin, we can't renew them at the current level, and then hiring slows down too because nobody's got room.

utterances.speaker: Wei
utterances.text: The renewals are quoted already.

utterances.speaker: Yuki
utterances.text: Right. So they'd be a problem. Concentrated, we protect those and the headcount lines.

utterances.speaker: Kofi
utterances.text: But travel and events, people are going to hate-

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: Kofi, I think maybe let her finish first.

utterances.speaker: Kofi
utterances.text: Sorry. She finished.

utterances.speaker: Yuki
utterances.text: I did, it's fine. He's not wrong, though, somebody's going to hate it.

utterances.speaker: Ivan
utterances.text: Some of the contractors are on projects mid-flight, I think.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: Is that, um, is that all of them?

utterances.speaker: Ivan
utterances.text: I don't know. Not all. Sione would know, he manages half of them.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: Right. We could ask him, I'd say.

utterances.speaker: Wei
utterances.text: Ask.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: I will. Um. After this. Or tomorrow. I'll put it in the notes so I don't lose it.

utterances.speaker: Yuki
utterances.text: I'll put it in the notes. I'm already writing.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: Thanks, Yuki.

utterances.speaker: Kofi
utterances.text: Can I switch to something totally different for a second? It's small.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: Is it on the, uh, on the list?

utterances.speaker: Kofi
utterances.text: It's not on the list. It's the expense thing.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: Okay, go on, but quickly.

utterances.speaker: Kofi
utterances.text: So the limit where it's just a manager signing off, it's five hundred. Above that it needs a second person. I think we raise it to a thousand.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: Why, um, why a thousand?

utterances.speaker: Kofi
utterances.text: Because those claims just sit. Between five hundred and a thousand, they wait about four days on average for the second signature.

utterances.speaker: Wei
utterances.text: How many get rejected?

utterances.speaker: Kofi
utterances.text: None. Last year, none at all in that range. I checked the log.

utterances.speaker: Ivan
utterances.text: Four days feels long for a taxi receipt.

utterances.speaker: Kofi
utterances.text: It's mostly conference fees and the odd flight change, but yeah.

utterances.speaker: Yuki
utterances.text: Oh, that's easy. Nobody's gaming that.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: Um, does finance control need to sign off on moving the number?

utterances.speaker: Kofi
utterances.text: Beatriz did, last month. Kind of. She said it was fine if we recommended it.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: Kind of.

utterances.speaker: Kofi
utterances.text: She said it in the corridor. I can email her to be sure.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: Okay, no, I think that's enough for me. The manager-only limit goes up to a thousand dollars.

utterances.speaker: Kofi
utterances.text: Great. I'll write it up and get the policy page changed.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: Tell Camille, she does the page.

utterances.speaker: Kofi
utterances.text: Right, Camille.

utterances.speaker: Ivan
utterances.text: Does it apply from today?

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: Um, let's say from the first of next month. Or, I mean, once the page is updated.

utterances.speaker: Kofi
utterances.text: The page is quick. I can do it this week.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: Good. Thanks.

utterances.speaker: Wei
utterances.text: Done?

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: Done, yeah. Back to the, the cut.

utterances.speaker: Yuki
utterances.text: Did anyone else see the thing about the new coffee place downstairs? Sorry, I know, tangent.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: Oh, I think maybe not right now-

utterances.speaker: Kofi
utterances.text: What thing?

utterances.speaker: Yuki
utterances.text: They're replacing the sandwich counter. Gabor was telling me, he's, um, he's going to miss the old one before he moves.

utterances.speaker: Kofi
utterances.text: He's still going to Rotterdam?

utterances.speaker: Yuki
utterances.text: March, yeah. He's packing already, apparently.

utterances.speaker: Ivan
utterances.text: He told me he's taking the standing desk.

utterances.speaker: Kofi
utterances.text: They won't let him.

utterances.speaker: Ivan
utterances.text: He said he already asked.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: Okay, okay. I think maybe we should-

utterances.speaker: Yuki
utterances.text: Sorry. Yes. Back.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: So, where, where do we stand on the cut? We have the flat one, and the, um, the targeted one.

utterances.speaker: Ivan
utterances.text: And the numbers are different now that we know about the contracts.

utterances.speaker: Wei
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: Kofi
utterances.text: I'd still want to see the targeted one by line. Not the idea. The dollars.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: Fair. Yuki, could you do that? Or, um, with Kofi's travel numbers?

utterances.speaker: Yuki
utterances.text: Yes. I can. I'm not great at the detail but I'll sit with Kofi.

utterances.speaker: Kofi
utterances.text: I'll send you what I have.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: And the file lock, I think it's still around the twentieth. I'd have to ask Beatriz.

utterances.speaker: Wei
utterances.text: Ask her today.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: Okay. Okay, today. I'll message her after this.

utterances.speaker: Ivan
utterances.text: I might need to leave in a few minutes, I have a thing at eleven.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: Oh, sure, of course. Is there anything else anyone needs from me?

utterances.speaker: Wei
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: Kofi
utterances.text: Just Esra on facilities.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: Friday. I'll nudge on Friday. Okay. Thanks, everyone.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: Okay, um, can everyone hear me? The speaker in this room has been, uh, crackly all week.

utterances.speaker: Kofi
utterances.text: Sounds fine. Ivan's here, Wei's here, Yuki's just sitting down.

utterances.speaker: Yuki
utterances.text: Here, sorry. The stairwell door was jammed, I had to go all the way round-

utterances.speaker: Wei
utterances.text: Start.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: Right. So, I think maybe we've gone round and round on the cut for two weeks, and I'd like to, you know, actually close it today.

utterances.speaker: Kofi
utterances.text: Finally.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: Before that, though. Esra, did she ever- no wait, I asked that last time. Did anyone hear from her?

utterances.speaker: Ivan
utterances.text: She wrote back Friday. Facilities is nearly all fixed. Rent, the cleaning contract. A little bit in maintenance.

utterances.speaker: Kofi
utterances.text: Told you. She doesn't reply before Wednesday and then it's a paragraph.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: Okay. So that's basically out either way.

utterances.speaker: Wei
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: Yuki
utterances.text: Which is sort of the big picture. Anything that's actually soft is the discretionary stuff, not the buildings.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: Mm. And I got to Sione, finally. About the contractors.

utterances.speaker: Kofi
utterances.text: And?

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: He said, um, around half of his people finish up by the end of March. The others are mid-project and he'd rather we leave them.

utterances.speaker: Ivan
utterances.text: So some room, but not all of it.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: Some, yeah.

utterances.speaker: Kofi
utterances.text: That's what I was saying last time, they can't all be-

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: Kofi, I think maybe let me finish. And Beatriz says the lock is the twenty-fourth. Not the twentieth.

utterances.speaker: Ivan
utterances.text: I did say the twenty-fourth.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: You did. You did, sorry, Ivan. I had it in my head as the twentieth.

utterances.speaker: Wei
utterances.text: Four more days.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: Which isn't a lot, honestly.

utterances.speaker: Yuki
utterances.text: Kofi, did the three lines come together? The ones from the sheet?

utterances.speaker: Kofi
utterances.text: I sent you travel. Events I pulled this morning. Contractors I kind of guessed from Sione's list.

utterances.speaker: Yuki
utterances.text: Got them. I put everything on one tab. It covers it, I think. Travel's the big chunk, events are, um, smaller.

utterances.speaker: Wei
utterances.text: How close.

utterances.speaker: Yuki
utterances.text: With contractors in it clears the number. Thirty thousand over? Something like that, I'd want to look again.

utterances.speaker: Kofi
utterances.text: It's closer to twenty-five, I had it on my-

utterances.speaker: Yuki
utterances.text: Okay, twenty-five. Still over.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: Okay. That's, um, that's helpful. That's good.

utterances.speaker: Kofi
utterances.text: Can I ask something totally unrelated? Who's doing the card for Gabor?

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: Oh. Is, um, is that going round already?

utterances.speaker: Kofi
utterances.text: Camille started one. It's on her desk, I think. Nobody's signed it.

utterances.speaker: Yuki
utterances.text: I haven't seen it. What are we getting him, a gift thing?

utterances.speaker: Kofi
utterances.text: A voucher, maybe. Something for the new place.

utterances.speaker: Ivan
utterances.text: He asked for a proper kettle. I'm not joking.

utterances.speaker: Yuki
utterances.text: A kettle. For Rotterdam.

utterances.speaker: Ivan
utterances.text: He said theirs are different.

utterances.speaker: Kofi
utterances.text: They are, they're the- never mind, I'll ask Camille what she's collecting.

utterances.speaker: Wei
utterances.text: How much each.

utterances.speaker: Kofi
utterances.text: Ten? Fifteen? She didn't say.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: Okay, okay. I think maybe we should come back. Sorry. Kofi, you can sort that out afterwards.

utterances.speaker: Kofi
utterances.text: Yep. Sorry.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: So. The flat one, versus aiming it. Does anyone, um, want to say anything that they haven't already?

utterances.speaker: Ivan
utterances.text: Um. I still think the flat one is easier to explain. That was my whole reason.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: It was a good reason. It is.

utterances.speaker: Ivan
utterances.text: But the thing Wei found changed it for me. If it's mostly landing on the stuff that's not locked anyway, then it isn't really even.

utterances.speaker: Wei
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: Yuki
utterances.text: And the tooling renewals. They come due in the second quarter, and the quotes are in. If everything uncommitted takes the hit, those are exposed.

utterances.speaker: Kofi
utterances.text: But the people running travel are going to be furious. Like, properly-

utterances.speaker: Yuki
utterances.text: Some people will be, yes.

utterances.speaker: Kofi
utterances.text: -furious, because they've got conferences booked already, half of them-

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: Booked or committed? There's a difference, isn't there.

utterances.speaker: Kofi
utterances.text: Booked and paid is committed. Booked but not paid, that's still in the uncommitted number.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: Right, okay. So that's in Yuki's figure already?

utterances.speaker: Yuki
utterances.text: I used the uncommitted column, so yes. I think. Kofi gave me the split.

utterances.speaker: Kofi
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: Wei
utterances.text: Fine.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: Um. Ivan, is there anything about the flat one that's still bothering you? You can say.

utterances.speaker: Ivan
utterances.text: No. Not really. I just don't want to be the one who, um. If a head complains.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: No, that's, that's mine to deal with. Not yours.

utterances.speaker: Ivan
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: Kofi
utterances.text: And if it's the flat one we get fifteen emails anyway.

utterances.speaker: Yuki
utterances.text: We'd get a different fifteen.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: Okay. I think maybe I've heard enough. Yeah. The cut goes on travel, contractors and events, only the uncommitted lines in those, adding up to the eight percent. Targeted, not across everyone.

utterances.speaker: Kofi
utterances.text: Good.

utterances.speaker: Wei
utterances.text: Done.

utterances.speaker: Yuki
utterances.text: Okay. Should I redo the sheet so it shows that and not the old version?

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: Yes, please. Um, with Kofi's final split, not the guess for the contractors.

utterances.speaker: Kofi
utterances.text: I'll get Sione to confirm his list this week.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: And the department heads need to hear before the lock. Um, this week, ideally. Before the weekend?

utterances.speaker: Wei
utterances.text: Who sends.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: I will. I'll draft it and you can all look at it. Maybe Thursday.

utterances.speaker: Yuki
utterances.text: Draft it tomorrow, we'll fix it Thursday.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: Yes. That works better.

utterances.speaker: Ivan
utterances.text: Should I take my table off the shared folder? So nobody opens the old one?

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: Um, rename it, maybe. Put old in the name.

utterances.speaker: Ivan
utterances.text: Okay. I'll do that.

utterances.speaker: Kofi
utterances.text: I have to go, I've got the vendor call at eleven.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: Oh, sure, go. Thanks, Kofi.

utterances.speaker: Kofi
utterances.text: And I'll find Camille about the card.

utterances.speaker: Wei
utterances.text: Bye.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: Okay. Thanks, everyone.

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: Okay, I think everyone's here. Diego, you made it, good.

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: Train was late. Sorry.

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: No problem. First thing, the Leeds fire door sign-off. Hedda said the contractor comes Thursday, not Wednesday.

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: Thursday works. I'll be on site.

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: Great. Elif, did the badge reader quote come through?

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: Um, I think so? Hamid forwarded something. Somewhere around the, the usual range.

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: The usual range being what, roughly? I have 2,300 in the budget line.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: I'd have to look. It was not wildly off, I remember that.

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: Right. Can you send it to me after this so I can compare against the line?

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: Sure, yes. Today.

utterances.speaker: Tomas
utterances.text: Is that the reader for the second floor entrance or the car park side?

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: Second floor. I think. Maybe both, actually.

utterances.speaker: Tomas
utterances.text: Well, that's a big difference in price.

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: Let's get the quote in front of us first. Okay, moving on. The cleaning contract in Leeds.

utterances.speaker: Marco
utterances.text: Yeah, um, so Brightwash is up at the end of this month, and they sent over the renewal terms last week.

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: Right, I've got the email here. Before you go on, they want an answer by the fourteenth, I believe.

utterances.speaker: Marco
utterances.text: Oh, is it the fourteenth? I thought it was the end of the month.

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: Fourteenth for the rate lock. After that they said the price goes back to list.

utterances.speaker: Marco
utterances.text: Okay. Good to know. That, that changes the timing a bit.

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: Which option are we looking at?

utterances.speaker: Marco
utterances.text: Well, so far just the one, really. I think maybe we should just renew them. Two years, six percent up on the current rate, so it comes to forty-four thousand a year.

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: Forty-four, so that's up from, what, a bit over forty-one?

utterances.speaker: Marco
utterances.text: Yeah, about forty-one and a half, I think.

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: Forty-one five-ish. Okay, six percent of that is, um, about twenty-five hundred. Roughly.

utterances.speaker: Tomas
utterances.text: And that's two years locked at that figure.

utterances.speaker: Marco
utterances.text: Yes, that's what they put in the email. Flat for both years.

utterances.speaker: Tomas
utterances.text: Hm. Devil's advocate, but what happens in year two if the market drops? We're stuck.

utterances.speaker: Marco
utterances.text: That's true, I suppose. But I mean, it's not like cleaning rates are going to fall.

utterances.speaker: Tomas
utterances.text: You never know.

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: They won't.

utterances.speaker: Tomas
utterances.text: Fine, fine. I just like to ask.

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: Marco, what's the argument for staying put, beyond not having to change anything?

utterances.speaker: Marco
utterances.text: So, I looked at the complaints log, the one the office team keeps. Over the last twelve months there were only eleven issues, and most were small, like a missed bin.

utterances.speaker: Marco
utterances.text: And I talked to Joao a bit about what a switch looks like. I think maybe three weeks of disruption, new people learning the floor plan, keys, alarm codes, all that.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: Three weeks is a long time though. People complain about everything in the first month.

utterances.speaker: Marco
utterances.text: Right, that's kind of my point.

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: Eleven in a year is about one a month. That's not nothing but it's not bad.

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: Seems fine to me.

utterances.speaker: Tomas
utterances.text: Eleven could also mean people stopped reporting. Has anybody checked whether staff still use the log?

utterances.speaker: Marco
utterances.text: Um, I don't know. I think they do. Bilal still sends stuff through.

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: Bilal's the one who chases the portal. I can ask him.

utterances.speaker: Tomas
utterances.text: I'm not saying it's wrong. Just that a quiet log isn't the same as a clean office.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: I mean, the big picture is we want something that doesn't need our attention, right? And Brightwash mostly doesn't.

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: Mostly. Let me look at the contract a second. There's a clause about the supplies, isn't there?

utterances.speaker: Marco
utterances.text: There's something about consumables. I think they bill those on top?

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: Section four, yes. Consumables are extra, capped at, um, eighteen hundred a year. Is that in the forty-four?

utterances.speaker: Marco
utterances.text: Honestly, I don't think so. I'd have to check.

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: Okay, that's one thing to pin down. I'll write it on my list.

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: Who do we ask?

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: Rui in procurement, probably. He handled the original.

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: Can I jump in with something else? Sorry, the desk booking thing.

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: Go ahead, quickly.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: People in Leeds keep saying the booking screen shows desks free that are already taken. Hedda mentioned it twice.

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: Is that a facilities problem or an IT one?

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: Um, both? I'd say it's the sync, which is IT, but we get the angry emails.

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: Forward them on.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: I did. Twice. Nothing happened.

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: Put it in the ticket system and tag me, I'll nudge Daan.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: Okay. Thanks.

utterances.speaker: Tomas
utterances.text: While we're on the Leeds office, did anyone sort the printer lease? It was due in March, I think.

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: That's this month. Diego, you had that one.

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: Yeah. Got two quotes. One's cheaper, one has toner included.

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: What's the gap?

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: Couple hundred a year. Not much.

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: I'd rather have toner included then. Fewer little invoices.

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: Fine.

utterances.speaker: Tomas
utterances.text: Not decided though, right? You're just saying you'd prefer it.

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: Right, just preferring. Send me the two numbers and we'll sort it by email.

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: Will do.

utterances.speaker: Marco
utterances.text: Sorry, back on the cleaners for a moment. Is there anything else people want me to find out?

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: A few things, yes. The consumables question, the log, and whether Bilal's team really uses it.

utterances.speaker: Marco
utterances.text: Okay, I'll write that down.

utterances.speaker: Tomas
utterances.text: And I'd like to know what a competitor would charge. Even a rough figure. Otherwise forty-four is just a number somebody gave us.

utterances.speaker: Marco
utterances.text: I mean, I can ask around. I don't have any other names, though.

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: Ask Joao. He mentioned a firm in Manchester once.

utterances.speaker: Marco
utterances.text: Oh, I think maybe I remember. Is that, uh, Northgate something?

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: Think so. Not sure.

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: I'm wary of dragging this out. The fourteenth is close, and I don't want to go in blind and lose the rate lock.

utterances.speaker: Tomas
utterances.text: Eleven days. We have time for a phone call.

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: A call, sure. But a full tender in eleven days, no.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: Nobody's suggesting a tender. Right?

utterances.speaker: Tomas
utterances.text: No, no. A ballpark.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: Good. Because the bigger thing is the whole Leeds lease conversation, and that'll take everyone's attention soon.

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: Is that going ahead? I haven't heard anything since January.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: I think there's a meeting. Hamid said something about a floor reduction.

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: Which would change the cleaning scope, wouldn't it.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: Exactly. Well, maybe. I don't know how much.

utterances.speaker: Marco
utterances.text: Oh. That would matter for a two year deal.

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: It might. Or it might be nothing. I'll ask Hamid, though I'd bet he doesn't know either.

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: Ask anyway.

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: Yes. Okay, so for the record, nothing's settled on the cleaners. The renewal is on the table, and we have homework.

utterances.speaker: Marco
utterances.text: Yeah, I'll do the consumables and the competitor call.

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: And I'll talk to Bilal and Hamid. Tomas, anything you want to take?

utterances.speaker: Tomas
utterances.text: I'll pull the old invoices so we can see what we really paid last year. Maybe there are extras hiding in there.

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: Good, thanks. That helps.

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: Can we do the fire door thing now? I'm confused about who unlocks Thursday.

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: Yes. Hedda said she'd be in at seven. She has the key.

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: And the alarm?

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: Rui has the code. Wait, no, it's Daan. Sorry, Daan.

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: You sure?

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: Pretty sure. I'll double check and tell you tonight.

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: Okay. I have to go in two minutes, by the way. Call at half past.

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: Fine. Anything else, quickly? Elif, the quote, remember.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: Yes, sending it right after.

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: Okay. Next time, same slot, same room. Thanks, all.

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: Okay, we're all here. Elif, the badge reader quote, did it land last week?

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: Yes. Um, I sent it Monday, I think. Maybe Tuesday.

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: Found it, Tuesday. Second floor only, 2,350 fitted. So fifty over the line.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: That's close enough, right?

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: It's close. I'll just absorb it.

utterances.speaker: Tomas
utterances.text: Fitted meaning they do the cabling too?

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: It says so. I'll confirm with them.

utterances.speaker: Tomas
utterances.text: Mm. Worth confirming, cabling is where they get you.

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: Printer lease is signed. Toner one.

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: Good. Thanks, Diego.

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: Courier brings the unit Thursday.

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: Thursday is also the fire door contractor. Is that going to clash?

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: Different floors. Fine.

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: Okay. Marco, the cleaners. Did Rui get back to you on the consumables?

utterances.speaker: Marco
utterances.text: Not yet, no. I think maybe he's out until Wednesday? I sent it twice though.

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: Fine, that stays open. The rate lock is Friday the fourteenth, so we've got four days after this.

utterances.speaker: Marco
utterances.text: Right, right. I have it written down this time.

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: Elif, you said you'd chase a couple of other firms. Anything come back?

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: Oh, yes. So, two quotes came in on Friday, actually. I meant to forward them.

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: Two.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: One was a lot higher, we can ignore that one. The other is Kestrel Facilities, and they came in under, forty-one a year.

utterances.speaker: Marco
utterances.text: Forty-one thousand? Against forty-four?

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: Yeah. And they put in credits if they miss a visit, and the contract can be left with ninety days' notice.

utterances.speaker: Tomas
utterances.text: Credits how? A discount or an actual refund?

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: Um, off the next invoice. I'd have to reread it.

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: Send me the PDF after this.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: Yes. And I rang three of their clients, they gave me names. None of them had missed a visit.

utterances.speaker: Tomas
utterances.text: None? Not one in how long?

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: A year or more, for two of them. The third was newer. I didn't push on that.

utterances.speaker: Marco
utterances.text: That's, well, that's quite good, I think.

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: Which kinds of clients? Offices?

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: Two offices and a clinic. Sorry, vague, I wrote it down somewhere.

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: Okay. Put it in the notes when you send the PDF.

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: Kestrel. We should move to them.

utterances.speaker: Marco
utterances.text: Uh, shouldn't we, um, look at it a bit more first?

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: Why?

utterances.speaker: Marco
utterances.text: I mean, we've only just seen it. I think maybe-

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: It's cheaper and it's got an exit.

utterances.speaker: Tomas
utterances.text: Hang on, make the case properly. Cheaper by how much, once you net out everything?

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: Three grand a year, against the renewal.

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: Forty-four less forty-one, yes. Three thousand.

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: And the exit's ninety days. If they're bad, we leave. Brightwash wants us in for two years. Kestrel does the handover with their own people, two weeks.

utterances.speaker: Tomas
utterances.text: That's fair. What about the changeover? Marco said three weeks of mess.

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: Like I said, two weeks.

utterances.speaker: Marco
utterances.text: Two weeks is still, you know, disruption.

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: Less than three.

utterances.speaker: Tomas
utterances.text: Devil's advocate, they could say two weeks and mean four.

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: Maybe. Then we use the exit.

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: Okay. I'm hearing it, but we're not deciding it today. I haven't read the contract.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: No, of course. It's just the big picture, it looks promising.

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: Looks promising, agreed. Marco, can you get Brightwash to hold the rate lock a few more days?

utterances.speaker: Marco
utterances.text: I can ask. I think maybe they'd say no, though.

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: Ask anyway.

utterances.speaker: Marco
utterances.text: Okay. Today.

utterances.speaker: Tomas
utterances.text: Also, what happened with Northgate? Did anyone call?

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: I think that was one of the quotes. Maybe the high one. I'd have to check the names.

utterances.speaker: Tomas
utterances.text: Right, so you don't know either.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: I'll check.

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: Fine. Moving on, because we have the recycling thing from the Leeds survey and I'd like to give it ten minutes.

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: The bins.

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: Yes. Facilities got complaints about the sorting. Tomas, you had a view?

utterances.speaker: Tomas
utterances.text: Um, yes. Get rid of the little bins at every desk. Put shared ones at each floor, by the kitchen and the printers.

utterances.speaker: Marco
utterances.text: Everyone would lose their own bin?

utterances.speaker: Tomas
utterances.text: Yes. Everyone.

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: People will grumble.

utterances.speaker: Tomas
utterances.text: They grumble at everything. Look at the numbers though. Cleaners spend thirty-five minutes a night going round the desk bins. A hundred and twenty of them.

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: Thirty-five minutes.

utterances.speaker: Tomas
utterances.text: Every night. And on the pilot floor, the fourth, contamination in the recycling went from thirty-one percent down to twelve.

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: Thirty-one to twelve. That was the audit figure, from January?

utterances.speaker: Tomas
utterances.text: Yes, the one the waste contractor did.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: And the pilot floor is happy?

utterances.speaker: Tomas
utterances.text: Mostly. One person asked for a bin back. Nobody else.

utterances.speaker: Marco
utterances.text: What would it cost, to buy the shared ones?

utterances.speaker: Tomas
utterances.text: Not much. I have a quote somewhere, a few hundred. I'd have to find it.

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: Fine, the cost doesn't change my mind. It's the cleaning minutes and the contamination. Go ahead and roll the shared floor bins out, and pull the desk ones.

utterances.speaker: Tomas
utterances.text: Great. When?

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: Next month, floor by floor. Diego, can you co-ordinate with Hedda?

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: Marco
utterances.text: Do we tell people first?

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: An email this week. Elif, can you draft that?

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: Sure. Short and friendly.

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: Good. Right, going back to the cleaners for one minute so nobody leaves confused.

utterances.speaker: Tomas
utterances.text: Nothing's decided there.

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: Nothing's decided. Two options, Brightwash at forty-four and Kestrel at forty-one, and I'm going to read the Kestrel terms tonight.

utterances.speaker: Marco
utterances.text: And I'll ask about the rate lock.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: And I'll send the PDF.

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: Anyone want to know my view again?

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: We know it, Diego.

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: Tomas
utterances.text: I'd like Kestrel to answer a couple of questions in writing, though. Insurance, the key handling.

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: Write them down and send them to me, I'll pass them on.

utterances.speaker: Tomas
utterances.text: Will do.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: Is it the same slot next week?

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: Same slot. Actually, Tuesday, I have something Monday.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: Tuesday. Noted.

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: Okay. Thanks, everyone.

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: Okay, cleaners first today, because that one has a clock on it. Everybody here? Elif, you're on mute.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: Sorry, sorry. Yes, here.

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: Good. So, I read the Kestrel contract last Tuesday night, all of it, and I have notes. Marco, where did you get to with Brightwash?

utterances.speaker: Marco
utterances.text: Um, so I asked about holding the rate. I think maybe they were annoyed, but they said they'd keep it until the end of this week.

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: Until Friday. Okay, that's something.

utterances.speaker: Marco
utterances.text: Yeah. They said it's a one-off, though. I think they were quite clear about that.

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: So four days.

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: Roughly, yes. Tuesday to Friday, if we count today as gone.

utterances.speaker: Tomas
utterances.text: And the consumables? Did Rui ever come back?

utterances.speaker: Marco
utterances.text: He did, Wednesday. So the forty-four doesn't include them. They're on top, up to the eighteen hundred cap, like Hana said.

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: So really it's closer to forty-five eight if they use the whole cap.

utterances.speaker: Marco
utterances.text: I think so, yes. Maybe they wouldn't use all of it.

utterances.speaker: Tomas
utterances.text: Last year's invoices, I pulled them. They billed about fourteen hundred in consumables. Bin liners, soap, the paper towels.

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: Fourteen hundred. So call it forty-five and a half for Brightwash in practice.

utterances.speaker: Tomas
utterances.text: Give or take. And Kestrel's forty-one, does that have supplies in it?

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: That's my question for the Kestrel contract as well. Section six, I think. Let me find it.

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: Hurry up.

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: I'm looking, Diego. Okay. Consumables included, sorry, they say included, with a fair-use sentence I don't love.

utterances.speaker: Tomas
utterances.text: What's fair use mean when it's at home?

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: Doesn't say. I'd want a number in there.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: Can I ask something a bit off-topic first? Is the lights thing on the third floor fixed? Hedda said the motion sensors are going on and off all day.

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: That's Daan's, isn't it? I thought the electrician was in last week.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: He was, but it's apparently worse.

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: Worse how?

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: People wave their arms to get the lights on. In meetings. That's what Hedda told me.

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: Right. Put that in the ticket system and tag Daan, please. I'll mention it when I speak to him tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: Okay. Will do.

utterances.speaker: Marco
utterances.text: Um, back on the cleaners, sorry. Did Tomas's questions to Kestrel get answered? The insurance and the keys?

utterances.speaker: Tomas
utterances.text: They did, in writing, Thursday. Public liability is five million, certificate attached. I checked the expiry and it's good until next January.

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: And keys?

utterances.speaker: Tomas
utterances.text: Numbered keys, signed out, kept in a locked box at their depot, not with the cleaners. If one goes missing they pay for the lock change.

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: That's more than Brightwash does.

utterances.speaker: Tomas
utterances.text: Brightwash has the supervisor carry all of them around, I think. Which, frankly, is not great.

utterances.speaker: Marco
utterances.text: Is that, um, true? I never saw that.

utterances.speaker: Tomas
utterances.text: Joao told me once. Not sure how current it is.

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: Don't hang a conclusion on it. Joao's memory of something from a couple of years ago.

utterances.speaker: Tomas
utterances.text: Fair.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: What I keep coming back to is, big picture, we have something that works and something that might work better. Isn't that the whole choice?

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: Pretty much, with the money on the side.

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: Kestrel's cheaper. Exit's ninety days.

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: I know your view, Diego.

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: Just saying.

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: So let me go through the contract points I flagged, and then we should be able to get somewhere. First, the term. Initial period is twelve months, then rolling, and the ninety days can be used any time after month three.

utterances.speaker: Marco
utterances.text: Month three? Not from the start?

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: Not from the start, no. There's a settling-in period. So you can't walk away in the first ninety days.

utterances.speaker: Marco
utterances.text: Oh. So that's, um, six months really, before we're out in the worst case.

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: Roughly, yes. If we gave notice on day ninety-one, we'd be gone by about day one eighty.

utterances.speaker: Tomas
utterances.text: Hang on, is that a problem? Because that's what Diego was selling as the safety net.

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: Still a safety net. Six months is not two years.

utterances.speaker: Tomas
utterances.text: Six months of a bad cleaner is a long time.

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: Six months of a bad cleaner we'd be paying less for.

utterances.speaker: Tomas
utterances.text: Ha. Fine.

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: Second, the credits. Missed visit, they credit one visit's worth against the next invoice. Not a refund. Elif, you asked about that, I think.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: Right, I did say off the next invoice. Did I say that right?

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: You did.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: Good. I wasn't sure.

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: Third, the changeover. Two weeks, their own team does the walkthrough, we hand over the alarm codes on day one. They want a named contact on our side.

utterances.speaker: Marco
utterances.text: That'd be me, I think. Or, well, someone.

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: We'll sort out who. Not the sticking point.

utterances.speaker: Tomas
utterances.text: What about the Brightwash notice period? Are we even allowed to leave at the end of this month?

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: Their current term ends the thirty-first. The renewal is optional, so we're fine. I checked that.

utterances.speaker: Tomas
utterances.text: Okay. Just checking, since people forget auto-renew clauses.

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: There isn't one. That I did read.

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: Can I ask about the lease thing? Hamid, the floor reduction. Did he say anything?

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: I rang him Friday. He said the lease review is still going, nothing before the summer, and he doesn't expect a decision on the floors before the autumn.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: So it could shrink, but not soon.

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: Right. And that's a plus for the shorter commitment, I'd say.

utterances.speaker: Marco
utterances.text: Because if the scope changes mid-contract with Brightwash we're stuck.

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: Well, we'd have to negotiate. With Kestrel we could leave.

utterances.speaker: Marco
utterances.text: I think maybe that's a good point. I hadn't thought about it that way.

utterances.speaker: Tomas
utterances.text: Let me do the devil's advocate bit. Brightwash we know. Eleven complaints in twelve months, small ones. Kestrel we know from three phone calls.

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: Three of their clients, yes.

utterances.speaker: Tomas
utterances.text: And one of them was fairly new. What do we really know about the new one?

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: I spoke to the contact again, actually. After the meeting. The newer one is a clinic and they've had them about five months, no missed visits.

utterances.speaker: Tomas
utterances.text: Five months. Okay. That's better than I assumed.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: I told you it was vague. It's in the notes now.

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: It is. I read them.

utterances.speaker: Tomas
utterances.text: And Bilal? Did you find out if the complaints log is real?

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: Yes, sorry, I forgot to report that. Bilal says the office team still logs everything, and he thinks eleven is honest. If anything, a couple of items went in twice.

utterances.speaker: Tomas
utterances.text: Then Brightwash's record is as good as it looked.

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: As good as it looked, and no better.

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: So it's decent. And Kestrel's cheaper.

utterances.speaker: Marco
utterances.text: Um, can I say something? I'm, I'm still a bit nervous about the three weeks of disruption. Even two.

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: I hear that. Joao's three weeks was his estimate for an unprepared handover. Kestrel's walkthrough is organised.

utterances.speaker: Marco
utterances.text: Yeah, okay. I think maybe I'm just worried about the first week.

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: The first week will be untidy whoever we pick. Not much we can do about it.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: We could put someone on site the first morning.

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: I'll do that. I'm there Thursdays anyway.

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: The start would be the first of April, not a Thursday, I think. Whatever. We'll find someone.

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: I'll swap.

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: Thanks. Okay, so the money. Brightwash at forty-four with the consumables on top, call it forty-five and a half. Kestrel at forty-one all in, once I get the fair-use wording tightened. That's, um, four and a half a year between them. Roughly.

utterances.speaker: Tomas
utterances.text: Over the first twelve months, anyway.

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: Over twelve, yes. Okay. I've read it, I've heard everyone, and I don't think more calls change much. Kestrel Facilities, then. We go with them for Leeds, and I'll ask for the supplies wording to be fixed before I sign anything.

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: Marco, can you let Brightwash know today, politely, and say thanks for holding the rate? I'll email Kestrel this afternoon.

utterances.speaker: Marco
utterances.text: Um, yes. Sure. I think maybe I'll phone rather than email. It's, it's a bit awkward.

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: Phone is nicer. Keep it short.

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: Good.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: Great, that's off the list then.

utterances.speaker: Tomas
utterances.text: Ask them to name the supervisor in writing, as well. Whoever is on our floor.

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: I'll put that in with the supplies wording.

utterances.speaker: Tomas
utterances.text: Thanks.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: Oh, one other thing, quickly. The recycling email, it went out Wednesday, and I've had eight replies already.

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: Eight. Complaints?

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: Mostly, yes. Two people want their bins back. Other six are, um, practical questions about batteries and coffee cups.

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: Fine, send the six practical ones to Diego, he's doing the rollout with Hedda.

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: Send them to me. I'll answer.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: Okay. And the two?

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: Reply politely and tell them the pilot floor was fine. Don't argue.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: Marco
utterances.text: I have to run to another call, I'm sorry, can I-

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: Go, go. Phone Brightwash after.

utterances.speaker: Marco
utterances.text: Will do. Thanks, everyone.

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: Okay. Same slot next week, and I'll send the Kestrel paperwork round when I have it.

utterances.speaker: Kofi
utterances.text: Okay, everyone's here. Sven, you wanted to kick off?

utterances.speaker: Sven
utterances.text: Uh, yeah, in a sec. First, did anyone else get the offsite invite as tentative? Mine's greyed out.

utterances.speaker: Meera
utterances.text: I think maybe it's confirmed? Sunita sent something yesterday, I think.

utterances.speaker: Kofi
utterances.text: Confirmed. Thursday, ten o'clock.

utterances.speaker: Zainab
utterances.text: Same room as last time? The one where the projector dies?

utterances.speaker: Kofi
utterances.text: Different room. Gabor got the other one sorted anyway.

utterances.speaker: Zainab
utterances.text: Huh. Progress.

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: Is lunch covered?

utterances.speaker: Kofi
utterances.text: Yes. Sione ordered already.

utterances.speaker: Meera
utterances.text: Oh good, because I think maybe I forgot to bring anything last time and, um, anyway.

utterances.speaker: Sven
utterances.text: Okay. So the CRM thing. Closing out opps.

utterances.speaker: Kofi
utterances.text: Go.

utterances.speaker: Sven
utterances.text: So right now a rep marks something won and, uh, it basically takes whatever. Stage, amount, close date, done.

utterances.speaker: Zainab
utterances.text: Which is how reps like it. Nobody wants a form.

utterances.speaker: Sven
utterances.text: Right, right. But what I'd like is, um - the close screen just refuses to save until eight fields are filled. Eight, not the whole form.

utterances.speaker: Meera
utterances.text: Which eight? I think maybe I saw a list somewhere.

utterances.speaker: Sven
utterances.text: It's in the doc I shared. Competitor, use case, champion name, and, uh, the usual ones on top of those.

utterances.speaker: Kofi
utterances.text: Doc's in the invite. Read it after.

utterances.speaker: Zainab
utterances.text: Hang on, why now? What broke?

utterances.speaker: Sven
utterances.text: So last quarter, the win-loss review. We tried to run it and it just - it stalled.

utterances.speaker: Sven
utterances.text: Of the hundred and forty deals we closed, fifty-seven had nothing in the competitor box. Blank. You can't say who we lose to with that many empty, and if the screen won't let them skip it, that goes away.

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: Fifty-seven. That's, what, forty percent?

utterances.speaker: Sven
utterances.text: Around that. Yeah.

utterances.speaker: Zainab
utterances.text: Okay but blank doesn't mean it's fixed. They'll type "n/a" and move on.

utterances.speaker: Sven
utterances.text: Sure, some will. But, I mean, blank is worse than n/a.

utterances.speaker: Zainab
utterances.text: Is it? n/a looks like data. Blank looks like a gap. At least blank is honest.

utterances.speaker: Meera
utterances.text: I think maybe that's a fair point? Although, um, the dropdown could have a "none known" option.

utterances.speaker: Sven
utterances.text: Yeah, that - that's more detail than I was thinking, but sure.

utterances.speaker: Kofi
utterances.text: Dropdown is a build question. Leave it.

utterances.speaker: Zainab
utterances.text: I'm just saying we'd be forcing eight things at the exact moment the rep wants to be done.

utterances.speaker: Sven
utterances.text: Which is the moment they actually remember the answers, no?

utterances.speaker: Zainab
utterances.text: Or the moment they guess.

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: Some of those fields they can't know at close. Champion name, maybe.

utterances.speaker: Kofi
utterances.text: Why not?

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: If the deal came through procurement, the rep may never have met the real champion. They'd fill in whoever.

utterances.speaker: Meera
utterances.text: That's true, I think. Rafael's last two were all procurement.

utterances.speaker: Sven
utterances.text: Well, the rep usually knows who pushed internally. Usually.

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: Usually.

utterances.speaker: Zainab
utterances.text: See, that's a guess.

utterances.speaker: Kofi
utterances.text: Fine. Noted. Keep going.

utterances.speaker: Sven
utterances.text: Can I, uh - the other thing is the use case. We can't even say what people are buying these for.

utterances.speaker: Meera
utterances.text: I think maybe marketing asked for that too? Aiko mentioned it.

utterances.speaker: Sven
utterances.text: Right, she did. For the case studies.

utterances.speaker: Zainab
utterances.text: So marketing gets a field and the reps get the homework.

utterances.speaker: Kofi
utterances.text: Marketing gets nothing unless the data's good. Same point.

utterances.speaker: Zainab
utterances.text: Okay, okay.

utterances.speaker: Meera
utterances.text: Sorry, can I ask something totally different? Is anyone sitting by the window now? Because Irina said the desks are moving.

utterances.speaker: Kofi
utterances.text: Facilities thing. Not us.

utterances.speaker: Sven
utterances.text: I heard the whole row by the printer goes.

utterances.speaker: Meera
utterances.text: Oh no, I like that row. I think maybe the light there is better.

utterances.speaker: Zainab
utterances.text: The light by the printer. Wow.

utterances.speaker: Meera
utterances.text: It is though.

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: They moved the plants last week and nobody said anything.

utterances.speaker: Sven
utterances.text: I thought those were fake.

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: They're real. Somebody waters them.

utterances.speaker: Kofi
utterances.text: Can we get back to the close fields.

utterances.speaker: Sven
utterances.text: Yes. Sorry. Where were we.

utterances.speaker: Zainab
utterances.text: Me being annoying about guesses.

utterances.speaker: Sven
utterances.text: Right. Okay, so what if reps can't fill a field, they can still, uh - no. Scratch that. That's the n/a thing again.

utterances.speaker: Zainab
utterances.text: See, you got there yourself.

utterances.speaker: Sven
utterances.text: I got there halfway.

utterances.speaker: Kofi
utterances.text: How long does it take a rep to fill eight fields?

utterances.speaker: Meera
utterances.text: I think maybe a minute? If they know it?

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: More like three, if they have to go look something up.

utterances.speaker: Kofi
utterances.text: Three minutes on a won deal. That's nothing.

utterances.speaker: Zainab
utterances.text: Times a hundred and forty deals a quarter, though.

utterances.speaker: Kofi
utterances.text: Seven hours a quarter across the whole team. I can live with that.

utterances.speaker: Zainab
utterances.text: Seven. Is it? Hundred forty times three is - four hundred twenty minutes. Okay, yeah, seven.

utterances.speaker: Sven
utterances.text: Told you, tiny.

utterances.speaker: Zainab
utterances.text: I didn't say it was huge. I said it was a forced guess.

utterances.speaker: Kofi
utterances.text: Noted twice now.

utterances.speaker: Meera
utterances.text: What about the loss side? Do the same fields apply when it's closed lost?

utterances.speaker: Sven
utterances.text: Not in this. That's separate, I'd say. Or - I don't know, I hadn't gotten to it.

utterances.speaker: Kofi
utterances.text: Won only. We can look at lost later.

utterances.speaker: Meera
utterances.text: Okay, I think maybe that makes sense.

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: Does it apply to deals already open?

utterances.speaker: Sven
utterances.text: Anything that closes after it goes live. Old ones stay the way they are.

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: Okay. That's fine then.

utterances.speaker: Zainab
utterances.text: And when does it go live, who builds it?

utterances.speaker: Kofi
utterances.text: Admin side. I'll ask Sione how long, it's a validation rule, shouldn't be long.

utterances.speaker: Sven
utterances.text: He did something like it for the renewals form.

utterances.speaker: Kofi
utterances.text: Right. That took him an afternoon.

utterances.speaker: Zainab
utterances.text: Fine. I'll stop being difficult in a minute.

utterances.speaker: Kofi
utterances.text: Take your time.

utterances.speaker: Zainab
utterances.text: One more. If a rep misses quota and blames the screen, that's on us.

utterances.speaker: Kofi
utterances.text: That's not going to happen. Three minutes.

utterances.speaker: Zainab
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: Meera
utterances.text: I do think the competitor one is the most useful, though. I think maybe the others could be softer.

utterances.speaker: Sven
utterances.text: But then we're back to half-filled.

utterances.speaker: Meera
utterances.text: Yeah. I know. I just said it.

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: I'd rather have all eight than argue over which three.

utterances.speaker: Kofi
utterances.text: Same.

utterances.speaker: Sven
utterances.text: That's kind of my whole point, honestly. Pick the set and stick with it.

utterances.speaker: Zainab
utterances.text: I still think we'll get junk in champion name. But the competitor numbers convinced me, I guess. Fifty-seven blanks is bad.

utterances.speaker: Kofi
utterances.text: Alright. Eight fields mandatory at close-won, starting once Sione has the rule built. That's what we're doing.

utterances.speaker: Sven
utterances.text: Great. Thanks.

utterances.speaker: Meera
utterances.text: Should I tell the reps or does Kofi?

utterances.speaker: Kofi
utterances.text: I'll send something. Short.

utterances.speaker: Meera
utterances.text: Okay, good, I think maybe they'd read it from you.

utterances.speaker: Zainab
utterances.text: Put the list in the message. Don't make them open a doc.

utterances.speaker: Kofi
utterances.text: Obviously.

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: Can I get the field list as a spreadsheet? I want to check the picklists.

utterances.speaker: Sven
utterances.text: Yeah, I'll export it after this.

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: Thanks.

utterances.speaker: Kofi
utterances.text: Anything else? Quick things only.

utterances.speaker: Meera
utterances.text: The offsite thing. Do we need to bring laptops?

utterances.speaker: Kofi
utterances.text: Laptop, yes. Charger, yes.

utterances.speaker: Meera
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: Sven
utterances.text: Is parking free there?

utterances.speaker: Kofi
utterances.text: Gabor said there's a lot. I don't know the price.

utterances.speaker: Zainab
utterances.text: I'm taking the train.

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: Me too.

utterances.speaker: Sven
utterances.text: Ugh, fine, I'll look it up.

utterances.speaker: Kofi
utterances.text: Okay. That's it. Go do real work.

utterances.speaker: Kofi
utterances.text: Okay, everyone's in. Sven, you've got the thing from last week?

utterances.speaker: Sven
utterances.text: Uh, yeah, in a sec. Did the offsite photos ever go out? Sunita said she'd-

utterances.speaker: Meera
utterances.text: I think maybe Friday? She said Friday, I think.

utterances.speaker: Kofi
utterances.text: Not this meeting.

utterances.speaker: Zainab
utterances.text: A little bit this meeting. I'm in three of them with my eyes shut.

utterances.speaker: Kofi
utterances.text: Ask Sunita.

utterances.speaker: Sven
utterances.text: Okay. Okay. So, the close screen. It's been live a while now, and-

utterances.speaker: Zainab
utterances.text: Three weeks, about.

utterances.speaker: Meera
utterances.text: Was it three? I thought Sione pushed it, um, the Monday after.

utterances.speaker: Kofi
utterances.text: He had it done early. Three weeks.

utterances.speaker: Meera
utterances.text: Okay. I think maybe I lost a week somewhere.

utterances.speaker: Sven
utterances.text: Right, so big picture, it's doing what we wanted. The screen won't let-

utterances.speaker: Zainab
utterances.text: Is it, though.

utterances.speaker: Sven
utterances.text: Well, I mean, I haven't really, uh, looked at the-

utterances.speaker: Kofi
utterances.text: Sven. Have you looked at anything?

utterances.speaker: Sven
utterances.text: Not in detail. Priya pulled something, I think?

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: Um. Yeah. I did, a bit.

utterances.speaker: Kofi
utterances.text: Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: So, the time it takes to log a close. Before the change the median was about two minutes.

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: Since then it's eleven. That's the median, not a few slow ones.

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: And twenty-three reps have been entering their closed deals late, some by days. Also around eighteen percent of deals have n/a or a dash sitting in the competitor box.

utterances.speaker: Meera
utterances.text: Eleven? I think maybe I misheard. Eleven minutes?

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: Eleven.

utterances.speaker: Sven
utterances.text: That's, uh, that's higher than I pictured.

utterances.speaker: Kofi
utterances.text: Three minutes was the number we used.

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: That was a guess. This is from the timestamps.

utterances.speaker: Zainab
utterances.text: Okay, can I -

utterances.speaker: Kofi
utterances.text: Hang on. Priya, the late ones. Which reps?

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: I have the list. I didn't want to put names up in front of everyone.

utterances.speaker: Kofi
utterances.text: Fair. Send it to me.

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: Sven
utterances.text: Is the late thing, um, because they're dodging the screen?

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: I think so. A couple told me they wait until Friday and do a batch.

utterances.speaker: Meera
utterances.text: I do that with expenses, honestly.

utterances.speaker: Zainab
utterances.text: Can I go now?

utterances.speaker: Kofi
utterances.text: Go.

utterances.speaker: Zainab
utterances.text: Right. So this is what I said last week, except now it's got numbers on it. We're getting junk. Eighteen percent placeholders, and that's only the ones you can spot by eye.

utterances.speaker: Zainab
utterances.text: And eleven minutes a close, work that out over a week. I get about forty minutes per rep, every week, filling in boxes for a report that isn't any better than it was.

utterances.speaker: Zainab
utterances.text: We swapped blanks for n/a. Same analysis, just slower.

utterances.speaker: Sven
utterances.text: Well, hang on. Eighteen is still way better than forty, though.

utterances.speaker: Zainab
utterances.text: Better than blank, sure. But n/a isn't a competitor.

utterances.speaker: Sven
utterances.text: But the rest are real, right?

utterances.speaker: Priya

utterances.text: Can we get to the crash? I've been staring at the dashboard all morning and it's-

utterances.speaker: Yuki

utterances.text: Store review on the hotfix took three days, I think.

utterances.speaker: Nadia
utterances.text: Two and a half by the timestamps. Either way that's the second one in two cycles that just sat there.

utterances.speaker: Jonas
utterances.text: The payment one was Android and the slow review. This is a different cause entirely.

utterances.speaker: Nadia
utterances.text: Different cause, same shape. Fixed in days, live for over a week.

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: Which is what I've been saying since, I mean, since the first week-

utterances.speaker: Nadia
utterances.text: You have. Okay, so yes, we open the cadence question again, properly this time and not in the last ten minutes of a call.

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: Finally.

utterances.speaker: Jonas
utterances.text: I'll say it though, I'm not sure the schedule is the culprit. The bug was in the build either way.

utterances.speaker: Jonas
utterances.text: Okay, that's a different question.

utterances.text: Wait, which ones are we actually comparing? I know the freeze one, and then there was the one with the percentages-
