utterances.text: The two-week train we're on now, and every-week releases with the staged rollout. Five percent, then twenty-five, then everyone, plus the switch to halt it.

utterances.speaker: Yuki
utterances.text: Right, that.

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: But weekly sounds like way more QA. Thirty hours a pass, times four a month-

utterances.speaker: Nadia
utterances.text: That's the number I'm not sure still holds. Mei, you did the smoke test work, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: Mei
utterances.text: Yeah. Um. Can I say something about that?

utterances.speaker: Nadia
utterances.text: Please.

utterances.speaker: Mei
utterances.text: That thirty was mostly people clicking through the smoke checks by hand. They run on their own now, and the whole suite finishes in about three hours.

utterances.speaker: Mei
utterances.text: And the five percent stage, with something like the upload crash, we'd have seen it within a day. Not on day eight.

utterances.text: Three hours? Not thirty?

utterances.speaker: Mei
utterances.text: Three. I ran it twice Friday to make sure.

utterances.speaker: Nadia
utterances.text: I saw the run on Friday, it was a little under three, actually.

utterances.speaker: Mei
utterances.text: Okay, yes. Roughly that.

utterances.speaker: Jonas
utterances.text: Devil's advocate. Who's watching the five percent? A day of data is only useful if somebody's looking at it.

utterances.speaker: Mei
utterances.text: The crash-free line is on the dashboard already. And the halt switch, someone just flips it.

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: Whoever's on-call, then.

utterances.speaker: Jonas
utterances.text: Which is Hana on a Saturday at two in the morning.

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: Not if it's above the page line, it won't even buzz me, we changed that-

utterances.text: Exactly, so who looks?

utterances.text: That's a fair hole. We'd have to name somebody. I don't think it's a reason to stay where we are, though.

utterances.speaker: Jonas
utterances.text: Fair. I just don't want it to turn into nobody's job.

utterances.speaker: Yuki
utterances.text: Can I ask about the Friday thing? Xavier's four o'clock builds, are those just gone, or-

utterances.text: They're gone either way, there's a build every week.

utterances.speaker: Yuki
utterances.text: Okay, I like that.

utterances.speaker: Nadia
utterances.text: Goran's sharing feature, by the way. Still end of September?

utterances.speaker: Jonas
utterances.text: Last I heard. It'd get a shot at the next week's release instead of waiting on a freeze.

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: Honestly the freeze part is what bugs me. Wednesday before, three days of nothing merging, and then it still breaks.

utterances.speaker: Nadia
utterances.text: The freeze did its job on the payment one. It was the waiting after that hurt.

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: Yeah, no, that's fair.

utterances.speaker: Jonas
utterances.text: What about store review? Weekly means a submission every week. If they reject one we've lost a week and a half.

utterances.text: Five rejections last quarter, and that was with no regression pass at all. I'd expect fewer now.

utterances.text: Two of those five were re-reviews, and that was a checklist thing. That's fixable.

utterances.speaker: Jonas
utterances.text: Hm. Okay.

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: Has Samir said anything about capacity? Three hours is nothing, but his people still have to read the results.

utterances.speaker: Nadia
utterances.text: He said the load is fine as long as the handoff is clean. I'm paraphrasing, I'll get it in writing.

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.text: This is making me think of Klara's team again, they went weekly on the web side last year and nobody even noticed after a month.

utterances.speaker: Jonas
utterances.text: They don't have a store reviewing them, Yuki.

utterances.speaker: Yuki
utterances.text: True. True. Still.

utterances.speaker: Nadia
utterances.text: Anything else against it, Jonas? Last chance for poking.

utterances.text: The halt switch. Has anyone actually tested it? Because a switch nobody's pressed is a wish.

utterances.text: I tried it on the test build last week. It stopped the rollout at the second stage, took under a minute.

utterances.speaker: Jonas
utterances.text: Under a minute. Good enough for me.

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: So are we doing it?

utterances.text: Yes. Weekly releases with the staged rollout, five, twenty-five, everyone, and the halt switch. The two-week train is done.

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: Good. Great.

utterances.text: I'll stop poking, then.

utterances.text: Does this mean the calendar entries come out? Jonas just put in all those Wednesdays.

utterances.text: I did, last week. Of course.

utterances.text: The doc with the skip rules goes too, I guess.

utterances.text: Probably, yeah. Let's not rewrite everything right now.

utterances.text: Out of roughly a hundred and ten. Finance said one-twelve, but a little of that's already spoken for.

utterances.text: So that's, what, forty percent-ish. On one event.

utterances.text: Well, yeah, but-

utterances.text: Please do, it's only five questions.

utterances.text: Okay, is everyone here? Diego, I can see you but I can't hear you.

utterances.text: Yep, thanks. So I've got the expo follow-up, and then the ad copy thing, which is bugging me.

utterances.speaker: Zainab
utterances.text: Which first?

utterances.text: Whichever. Elif, you had your hand up?

utterances.text: Yeah, sorry, it's about the expo, so it probably belongs first anyway. I emailed the organiser last week because the registration counter on their site looked really flat to me.

utterances.text: So we pay forty-six thousand for a smaller room, and the people we most wanted to meet aren't in it. That's poor value.

utterances.text: Fine.

utterances.text: I'll send it right after this.

utterances.text: Thanks. Okay. Ad copy.

utterances.speaker: Ingrid
utterances.text: About that. Maybe a few more if you're generous. The rest are, um, conglomerates and a couple of holding companies.

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: Which fifty, roughly? Do you have the list?

utterances.speaker: Ingrid
utterances.text: In the sheet. I can send it.

utterances.speaker: Ravi
utterances.text: Fifty is still fifty. Who gets the weird ones?

utterances.speaker: Ingrid
utterances.text: I think maybe by where most of the revenue sits? Or - I haven't thought that all the way through.

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: Revenue by company from billing, that's easy enough to pull.

utterances.speaker: Marco
utterances.text: Wait, how many reps per sector, if there's three?

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: Six reps, three sectors. Two each.

utterances.speaker: Marco
utterances.text: Right, right, I knew that, I was just, yeah.

utterances.speaker: Ravi
utterances.text: And the half-timer? Sanne.

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: Until December. She'd pair with someone on a sector.

utterances.speaker: Pavel
utterances.text: Sanne's a detail. Anyone against?

utterances.speaker: Ravi
utterances.text: Honestly, I was arguing so someone would. It's cleaner than my tagging idea.

utterances.speaker: Marco
utterances.text: And the travel thing goes away, nobody's driving round postcodes.

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: Doubling up could come back though, two reps in one sector, same buyer.

utterances.speaker: Ingrid
utterances.text: Maybe they'd split by account name? Named, so one owner per account, not shared.

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: Named accounts, yes, each one has an owner. That's the point.

utterances.speaker: Ingrid
utterances.text: Oh. Right. I said it twice.

utterances.speaker: Pavel
utterances.text: Okay. Mid-market goes to named-account assignment across the three verticals, healthcare, financial services and public sector, two reps each. Postcodes are out.

utterances.speaker: Marco
utterances.text: Nice.

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: I'll rebuild the account list. Weekend again?

utterances.speaker: Pavel
utterances.text: Give me a date, not a weekend.

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: Friday. Draft list Friday.

utterances.speaker: Pavel
utterances.text: Fine. Ingrid, send him the fifty.

utterances.speaker: Ingrid
utterances.text: Today. Yes.

utterances.speaker: Ravi
utterances.text: The first of November, does that still stand?

utterances.speaker: Pavel
utterances.text: Don't know yet. Quota change is January. I'll look at it.

utterances.speaker: Ravi
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: Marco
utterances.text: Can I just say, I'm a bit relieved, the postcode thing had a lot of edge cases.

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: It had the boundary thing, and registered versus billing address.

utterances.speaker: Marco
utterances.text: Which we never answered.

utterances.speaker: Pavel
utterances.text: Doesn't matter now.

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: Matters for the fifty, actually. Billing and registered industry codes can differ.

utterances.speaker: Ingrid
utterances.text: Oh, I think I used the one on the account page. Which, maybe that's billing?

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: Probably. I'll compare when you send the list.

utterances.speaker: Pavel
utterances.text: Do that offline.

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: Offline, yeah.

utterances.speaker: Ravi
utterances.text: Did Marisol add the dropdown? The territory field.

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: She did, Thursday. It's sitting there with six postcodes in it.

utterances.speaker: Marco
utterances.text: Ha. Wasted.

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: Ask her to swap in the sectors?

utterances.speaker: Pavel
utterances.text: Ask her. And ask whether comp is affected, before anyone else does.

utterances.speaker: Ingrid
utterances.text: I think maybe comp would follow the quota thing, so - sorry, that's hers.

utterances.speaker: Pavel
utterances.text: Right, hers.

utterances.speaker: Marco
utterances.text: Speaking of Marisol, she told me her flat's been without heating for two weeks, and the landlord keeps sending, I swear, a different guy each time, one of them just stood in the hall and said it was "a pressure thing" and left, and then the next week -

utterances.speaker: Ravi
utterances.text: Marco, we're on a clock.

utterances.speaker: Marco
utterances.text: Sure. But the guy honestly just left.

utterances.speaker: Pavel
utterances.text: Poor Marisol. Hedda still wants to sit in on the next one.

utterances.speaker: Marco
utterances.text: Is that Tuesday?

utterances.speaker: Pavel
utterances.text: Monday. Same as always.

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: Monday I'm on a call till eleven.

utterances.speaker: Pavel
utterances.text: Join late.

utterances.speaker: Ravi
utterances.text: Can we move it to the afternoon?

utterances.speaker: Pavel
utterances.text: Hedda's only free in the morning.

utterances.speaker: Ravi
utterances.text: Fine. Morning.

utterances.speaker: Ingrid
utterances.text: Should I invite Tomasz too? Since it touches his accounts?

utterances.speaker: Pavel
utterances.text: Sure, invite him.

utterances.speaker: Ingrid
utterances.text: Okay. I think he's out Monday though, so maybe just forward the notes.

utterances.speaker: Pavel
utterances.text: Forward the notes.

utterances.speaker: Marco
utterances.text: Do I bin the email template then?

utterances.speaker: Pavel
utterances.text: Rewrite it for sectors. Short. I have to jump, Olivier's waiting.

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: Go, we're done.

utterances.speaker: Ravi
utterances.text: Okay, let's get started. Is everyone on? Kofi, I think you're still muted.

utterances.speaker: Kofi
utterances.text: Sorry, yeah, I'm here. Can you hear me now?

utterances.speaker: Ravi
utterances.text: Yep. So first, the Q4 quota sheets went out Friday, and Gabor says a couple of you haven't opened them.

utterances.speaker: Sofia
utterances.text: I think maybe I haven't? I saw the email, but I didn't, um, click through yet.

utterances.speaker: Ravi
utterances.text: Please do it today. It's forty-one rows per rep, it's not a lot.

utterances.speaker: Omar
utterances.text: Mine's done. Well, mostly done. There's one account under the wrong territory but I'll ping Gabor about it.

utterances.speaker: Ravi
utterances.text: Good.

utterances.speaker: Kwame
utterances.text: I opened it. It's fine.

utterances.speaker: Ravi
utterances.text: Thanks, Kwame. Next, the offsite room. Klara needs a headcount by Thursday.

utterances.speaker: Kofi
utterances.text: Is that the one in Leeds? Or no, that was last year.

utterances.speaker: Ravi
utterances.text: Manchester this year. Eight of us, if everyone comes.

utterances.speaker: Omar
utterances.text: Manchester's great, there's this place by the station that does the, uh - sorry, never mind. Eight, yes.

utterances.speaker: Sofia
utterances.text: I think maybe I can't do the Wednesday? Let me check my calendar.

utterances.speaker: Ravi
utterances.text: Just tell Klara directly, don't route it through me.

utterances.speaker: Sofia
utterances.text: Okay, will do.

utterances.speaker: Ravi
utterances.text: Right. Now the thing I actually wanted time for, the inbound leads. Omar, you had something.

utterances.speaker: Omar
utterances.text: Yeah, so, um. I've been looking at how the leads come in and who gets them, and honestly it's-

utterances.speaker: Ravi
utterances.text: Hang on, Kofi, you were saying something?

utterances.speaker: Kofi
utterances.text: No, no, go ahead. I just bumped my mic.

utterances.speaker: Omar
utterances.text: So right now Marisol, or whoever's on the queue that day, eyeballs the new ones and hands them out by hand.

utterances.speaker: Ravi
utterances.text: Right, that's the current setup. She does it in the morning and again after lunch, roughly.

utterances.speaker: Omar
utterances.text: Which is the problem, kind of. What if every inbound just went round-robin, one after another, across all six of us?

utterances.speaker: Kwame
utterances.text: All six inside reps?

utterances.speaker: Omar
utterances.text: Yeah, all six. Everybody in the rotation, no special lists.

utterances.speaker: Kofi
utterances.text: So like, it just deals them out. Like cards.

utterances.speaker: Omar
utterances.text: Sort of, yeah. Next lead goes to the next person in line.

utterances.speaker: Sofia
utterances.text: I think maybe that could work? I mean, depending on the, um, the way the territories are set.

utterances.speaker: Ravi
utterances.text: What are you comparing it to, Omar? Do we have actual numbers on the wait?

utterances.speaker: Omar
utterances.text: I pulled the timestamps last week. Lead created versus the first call or email. The middle one sits around five hours before anyone touches it.

utterances.speaker: Ravi
utterances.text: Five hours median. Not average.

utterances.speaker: Omar
utterances.text: Median. The average is worse, there's a long tail, some sit overnight.

utterances.speaker: Ravi
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: Omar
utterances.text: And with the rotation it's instant, the system assigns on creation. I tried it on last month's data and the first touch would come in under half an hour.

utterances.speaker: Kwame
utterances.text: That assumes we answer within half an hour.

utterances.speaker: Omar
utterances.text: Fair, yeah. But at least it'd be sitting in someone's own queue and not in a pile.

utterances.speaker: Sofia
utterances.text: Right, because now it's nobody's, really.

utterances.speaker: Omar
utterances.text: And the other thing, it comes out even. Right now Vikram gets slammed on Mondays and I'm sitting here with three leads.

utterances.speaker: Ravi
utterances.text: You had four last week, I looked.

utterances.speaker: Omar
utterances.text: Four. Okay. Still.

utterances.speaker: Kofi
utterances.text: The big picture is, we're leaving money on the table when they wait that long, right? People go cold.

utterances.speaker: Ravi
utterances.text: Roughly, yes. I don't have a conversion-by-wait figure in front of me.

utterances.speaker: Kofi
utterances.text: I mean, I remember something from a webinar. Like, the odds drop off a cliff after the first hour. Something like that.

utterances.speaker: Ravi
utterances.text: I'd want to see our own data before quoting that.

utterances.speaker: Kofi
utterances.text: Sure, sure.

utterances.speaker: Omar
utterances.text: I can pull ours too. It's a separate query though.

utterances.speaker: Ravi
utterances.text: Not needed for today.

utterances.speaker: Sofia
utterances.text: Can I ask, um, what happens when someone's out? Like if I'm on leave.

utterances.speaker: Omar
utterances.text: The tool skips anyone marked away. There's a toggle on the user record.

utterances.speaker: Sofia
utterances.text: Okay. I think maybe somebody should check that it actually works? Because in the old setup it didn't.

utterances.speaker: Omar
utterances.text: Yeah, I'll test it with a dummy user first.

utterances.speaker: Ravi
utterances.text: Do that.

utterances.speaker: Kwame
utterances.text: How many leads a day are we even talking about?

utterances.speaker: Ravi
utterances.text: Last quarter it was about sixty-something a day. Call it sixty-five, give or take. Split six ways, that's, uh, ten or eleven each.

utterances.speaker: Kwame
utterances.text: Ten or eleven. Okay, manageable.

utterances.speaker: Omar
utterances.text: It's more on campaign days. After the trade show it was double that for a week.

utterances.speaker: Ravi
utterances.text: True. The webinar in November will do it again.

utterances.speaker: Kofi
utterances.text: Oh, is Yara still running that one?

utterances.speaker: Ravi
utterances.text: Yara's running it, yes. Date isn't locked. That's separate, let's not get into it.

utterances.speaker: Kofi
utterances.text: Sorry, yeah.

utterances.speaker: Omar
utterances.text: Speaking of Yara, did anybody get the invite for her thing on Thursday? Because mine came twice.

utterances.speaker: Sofia
utterances.text: I got it twice too.

utterances.speaker: Kwame
utterances.text: Three times.

utterances.speaker: Ravi
utterances.text: It's a calendar glitch, ignore the duplicates.

utterances.speaker: Omar
utterances.text: Okay good, I was about to accept both and double-book myself.

utterances.speaker: Ravi
utterances.text: Back to leads. Anyone have a problem with how Omar laid it out?

utterances.speaker: Kwame
utterances.text: Not really.

utterances.speaker: Sofia
utterances.text: I think maybe, um, there's one thing. The rotation doesn't care how big the account looks. A little firm gets the same attention as a big one.

utterances.speaker: Omar
utterances.text: Right, every lead goes in the same line. That's the point of it.

utterances.speaker: Sofia
utterances.text: Okay. I was just, you know, noting it.

utterances.speaker: Ravi
utterances.text: Noted. Kofi?

utterances.speaker: Kofi
utterances.text: I think directionally it's right. Faster response, fairer split. I don't need more than that.

utterances.speaker: Ravi
utterances.text: Fine.

utterances.speaker: Omar
utterances.text: And honestly it takes maybe an hour to set up. The assignment rule is already in the CRM, it's just turned off.

utterances.speaker: Ravi
utterances.text: Who turned it off?

utterances.speaker: Omar
utterances.text: Sergei, I think, back when we had eight people and the territories were different. It's a checkbox plus a list of names.

utterances.speaker: Ravi
utterances.text: And that list would need the six of you in it.

utterances.speaker: Omar
utterances.text: Yeah, six. I'd check the names against the roster so nobody's left out.

utterances.speaker: Ravi
utterances.text: Make sure Marisol knows before it flips, so she stops handing things out by hand and doubles up.

utterances.speaker: Omar
utterances.text: Yeah, I'll message her today.

utterances.speaker: Kwame
utterances.text: Will she still see the queue?

utterances.speaker: Omar
utterances.text: She'll still see everything. She just won't have to move it.

utterances.speaker: Kwame
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: Ravi
utterances.text: All right. Omar, then have it running for Monday.

utterances.speaker: Omar
utterances.text: Monday, got it. I'll flip it Sunday night so it's clean.

utterances.speaker: Ravi
utterances.text: Not Sunday night, nobody will be watching it. Early Monday, before nine, and you stay on it.

utterances.speaker: Omar
utterances.text: Okay, early Monday. I'll be on at eight.

utterances.speaker: Sofia
utterances.text: Do we need to tell the reps, I mean, ourselves? Like an email?

utterances.speaker: Ravi
utterances.text: I'll write two lines to the group. Nothing formal.

utterances.speaker: Kofi
utterances.text: Should I tell my accounts that their leads might come from different people now?

utterances.speaker: Ravi
utterances.text: Your accounts aren't inbound, Kofi, they're existing. This doesn't touch them.

utterances.speaker: Kofi
utterances.text: Oh. Right. Okay.

utterances.speaker: Omar
utterances.text: Yeah, it's only new inbound.

utterances.speaker: Ravi
utterances.text: Okay. Anything else before we stop? I've got a hard stop at the half hour.

utterances.speaker: Kwame
utterances.text: One thing, the laptop refresh. Is that still happening in November?

utterances.speaker: Ravi
utterances.text: I think so. Sergei would know. Ask him directly.

utterances.speaker: Kwame
utterances.text: Will do.

utterances.speaker: Sofia
utterances.text: I think maybe I should also ask about the headset? Mine's crackling.

utterances.speaker: Ravi
utterances.text: Put it in the IT ticket, mention the model number.

utterances.speaker: Sofia
utterances.text: Okay, thanks.

utterances.speaker: Omar
utterances.text: Quick thing, I found the best coffee place near the Manchester venue, I'm sending a link-

utterances.speaker: Ravi
utterances.text: Send it in chat, I've got to jump. Thanks everybody.

utterances.speaker: Omar
utterances.text: Yep, will do.

utterances.speaker: Kofi
utterances.text: Thanks, Ravi.

utterances.speaker: Pavel
utterances.text: Okay. Everyone here? Ingrid, you're on mute.

utterances.speaker: Ingrid
utterances.text: Sorry, I think maybe - better now?

utterances.speaker: Pavel
utterances.text: Better. Draft account list. Diego, where is it?

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: Went out Friday like I said. Three hundred and sixty clean ones sorted by sector, plus the fifty Ingrid sent, which I've been working through.

utterances.speaker: Pavel
utterances.text: And the fifty?

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: Mostly placed. I used billing revenue to pick the sector for the conglomerates, so whichever business line brings in the most money.

utterances.speaker: Ravi
utterances.text: Most by what margin? A fifty-one, forty-nine split is not really a call.

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: Right, there are about seven like that. I flagged them in yellow.

utterances.speaker: Pavel
utterances.text: Seven. Who decides those?

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: I'd say you, or whoever we agree on. I just don't want to guess.

utterances.speaker: Ingrid
utterances.text: Could maybe the two reps from the sectors in question talk it through? I think maybe that's fairer than one person choosing.

utterances.speaker: Ravi
utterances.text: Fairer, sure. Slower too. They'll both want the bigger one.

utterances.speaker: Pavel
utterances.text: Diego, send me the seven. I'll look.

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: Today.

utterances.speaker: Marco
utterances.text: Did anyone see the thing with the registered office versus billing address? Because I looked at three of the yellow ones and the registered one is in a completely different country, I mean one of them is in Ireland, which, you know, tax reasons -

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: That's the same issue. The industry code on billing and on the registered record disagree for about a tenth.

utterances.speaker: Marco
utterances.text: A tenth of the fifty or a tenth of everything?

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: Everything. Roughly forty-ish accounts. I compared them last night.

utterances.speaker: Pavel
utterances.text: Which one wins?

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: Billing, I'd say. It's what finance uses to invoice, so it's the one that's kept current.

utterances.speaker: Pavel
utterances.text: Fine. Billing. Write it in the doc.

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: Done, I'll put it at the top.

utterances.speaker: Ravi
utterances.text: What happens to accounts where the billing code is wrong? Somebody's going to find a hospital filed as retail.

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: Then they tell me and I move it. It's a spreadsheet.

utterances.speaker: Ravi
utterances.text: Until it's in the CRM.

utterances.speaker: Pavel
utterances.text: Marisol. Where's she at on the dropdown?

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: Haven't heard back since Thursday. She's got something else going on with the quota memo.

utterances.speaker: Marco
utterances.text: Speaking of which, has anyone read the whole memo? Because page four has a bit about what counts as a closed deal and I think they changed -

utterances.speaker: Pavel
utterances.text: Marco. Dropdown.

utterances.speaker: Marco
utterances.text: Sorry. Yes. Dropdown.

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: I'll chase her again after this.

utterances.speaker: Pavel
utterances.text: Do it. It needs to be live before anyone's moved into it.

utterances.speaker: Ingrid
utterances.text: Do we know yet if November first still holds? I think maybe we said you'd look at it.

utterances.speaker: Pavel
utterances.text: I looked. Quota change is January, so there's no reason to rush. I want the lists clean first. Mid-November.

utterances.speaker: Ingrid
utterances.text: Oh, that's - that actually helps a lot with the handover notes.

utterances.speaker: Marco
utterances.text: I rewrote the intro email for sectors, by the way. Short, like you said. Three lines.

utterances.speaker: Pavel
utterances.text: Send it round.

utterances.speaker: Marco
utterances.text: It's in the shared folder. The version with the Friday date, ignore that one.

utterances.speaker: Ravi
utterances.text: What does it say about who the customer's new contact is?

utterances.speaker: Marco
utterances.text: The rep's name and the sector. Oh, and a line saying the old rep is still reachable till the end of the month.

utterances.speaker: Ravi
utterances.text: That's a promise. Some of us will be on leave.

utterances.speaker: Pavel
utterances.text: Then it's the old rep's problem. Change it to "for a transition period."

utterances.speaker: Marco
utterances.text: Okay, fine, vague is safer.

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: Sanne, what's the plan for her? She's half-time until December.

utterances.speaker: Pavel
utterances.text: Pairs with someone. Healthcare, I'd say, it's the biggest.

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: Healthcare has about a hundred and fifty. I've got it written down somewhere, one-fifty-something.

utterances.speaker: Ravi
utterances.text: Who's the other healthcare rep then?

utterances.speaker: Pavel
utterances.text: Hedda. I'll ask her.

utterances.speaker: Ingrid
utterances.text: Hedda wanted to come to these, didn't she? Should I maybe loop her in on the list?

utterances.speaker: Pavel
utterances.text: Send her the sheet, not the whole chain.

utterances.speaker: Ingrid
utterances.text: Okay. Just the sheet.

utterances.speaker: Marco
utterances.text: Can we do the expenses now, since we're all here? Mine's pending and I don't know why.

utterances.speaker: Pavel
utterances.text: Who approves?

utterances.speaker: Marco
utterances.text: Olivier, I think. Or finance.

utterances.speaker: Pavel
utterances.text: Check with Olivier. I haven't seen it.

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: Mine was approved Monday. Receipts were photos, they were fine.

utterances.speaker: Ravi
utterances.text: Mine's in. I'd like that on record.

utterances.speaker: Pavel
utterances.text: Noted. Thursday night or Friday morning?

utterances.speaker: Ravi
utterances.text: Tuesday, actually.

utterances.speaker: Pavel
utterances.text: Wow.

utterances.speaker: Marco
utterances.text: Growth.

utterances.speaker: Ingrid
utterances.text: Is the offsite still the fifteenth? I never got a straight answer.

utterances.speaker: Pavel
utterances.text: It was moved to the twenty-second. Daan sent a note.

utterances.speaker: Ingrid
utterances.text: Oh, I missed that. I think maybe it went to a folder.

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: I have it. Twenty-second, venue's the same one near the station.

utterances.speaker: Marco
utterances.text: So the train is a different price. I'll need to rebook, which is annoying because I found a really good fare -

utterances.speaker: Pavel
utterances.text: Marco.

utterances.speaker: Marco
utterances.text: Booking now. Sorry.

utterances.speaker: Ravi
utterances.text: Back to the lists for a second. When do the reps actually see their accounts?

utterances.speaker: Pavel
utterances.text: Once the seven are placed and the dropdown's live. I want one more pass from Diego.

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: I can do Monday if the seven are settled by the weekend.

utterances.speaker: Pavel
utterances.text: They will be.

utterances.speaker: Ingrid
utterances.text: Should we maybe give reps a day to check their own accounts before it's final? Just in case something looks off?

utterances.speaker: Pavel
utterances.text: A day. Not a week.

utterances.speaker: Ingrid
utterances.text: Yes, a day is fine. I just thought -

utterances.speaker: Pavel
utterances.text: Good idea. Write it in.

utterances.speaker: Ravi
utterances.text: What about open deals? If someone's mid-negotiation and the account moves.

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: Open opportunities stay with the original rep until close. That's the rule we used last time.

utterances.speaker: Ravi
utterances.text: Last time was a smaller reshuffle.

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: True. Doesn't change the rule though.

utterances.speaker: Pavel
utterances.text: Keep the rule. Anyone with a big open one, tell me.

utterances.speaker: Marco
utterances.text: I've got two. Neither's big. One's a clinic group, the other's, um, I don't remember, a logistics company I think.

utterances.speaker: Pavel
utterances.text: Logistics isn't one of the three.

utterances.speaker: Marco
utterances.text: Right, so that's one of the fifty, probably.

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: Probably. Tell me the name and I'll check where I put it.

utterances.speaker: Marco
utterances.text: After this.

utterances.speaker: Pavel
utterances.text: Tomasz. He's out Monday, right?

utterances.speaker: Ingrid
utterances.text: I think so. I forwarded the notes already.

utterances.speaker: Pavel
utterances.text: Good. Anything else?

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: Dropdown, seven accounts, Monday pass. That's mine.

utterances.speaker: Pavel
utterances.text: Right. I have to go, Olivier's waiting.

utterances.speaker: Ravi
utterances.text: Go, we're done.

utterances.speaker: Ravi
utterances.text: Okay, is everyone here? Omar, you're on mute.

utterances.speaker: Omar
utterances.text: Sorry, yeah. Here now.

utterances.speaker: Ravi
utterances.text: Good. Before anything else, Gabor wants the quota sheet corrections by end of day tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: Kofi
utterances.text: Is that the one with the territory fixes?

utterances.speaker: Ravi
utterances.text: That one. If a row is wrong, send him the account name, not a screenshot of the whole sheet.

utterances.speaker: Omar
utterances.text: I sent mine Monday. Did he, uh, did he actually get it?

utterances.speaker: Ravi
utterances.text: He did. He said the Monday one was fine.

utterances.speaker: Omar
utterances.text: Okay good.

utterances.speaker: Kwame
utterances.text: Mine's fine.

utterances.speaker: Ravi
utterances.text: Right. So it's been about two weeks since the rotation went on. Sofia, you were going to look at the lead data.

utterances.speaker: Sofia
utterances.text: I think maybe I did a first pass? I'm not sure it's, um, totally clean yet.

utterances.speaker: Ravi
utterances.text: That's fine. Just tell us what you've got.

utterances.speaker: Sofia
utterances.text: So, we had 640 inbound over the two weeks, and when I matched them against the account list, 112 of them were already somebody's account. Like, an existing customer filled in a form.

utterances.speaker: Ravi
utterances.text: A hundred twelve out of six-forty. That's, what, a bit under a fifth.

utterances.speaker: Sofia
utterances.text: I think maybe yes, around that. And then I looked at who called them. For 31 of those, a second rep phoned the same day, the owner and then whoever the rotation gave it to.

utterances.speaker: Omar
utterances.text: Thirty-one, huh.

utterances.speaker: Sofia
utterances.text: And there were five complaints. Customers writing in, um, saying they'd just spoken to someone else from us.

utterances.speaker: Ravi
utterances.text: Five complaints to who?

utterances.speaker: Sofia
utterances.text: Mostly to the account owners directly. One went to support, I think maybe.

utterances.speaker: Kofi
utterances.text: Five's not many, though, in the big picture.

utterances.speaker: Kwame
utterances.text: It's five we know about.

utterances.speaker: Ravi
utterances.text: Kwame, go on.

utterances.speaker: Kwame
utterances.text: It's, um. The rotation doesn't look at who owns what. It's walking straight over relationships people have built for years, and the customer gets called twice.

utterances.speaker: Omar
utterances.text: Yeah, but I mean, those are the exceptions. Most of the six-forty are net new, and those got touched in under half an hour like I said.

utterances.speaker: Kwame
utterances.text: I'm not arguing about the new ones.

utterances.speaker: Omar
utterances.text: No, I know. I'm just saying the speed thing is real. I checked the median last Friday and it's around, I don't know, forty minutes now?

utterances.speaker: Ravi
utterances.text: Forty minutes. Down from five hours, so that's not nothing.

utterances.speaker: Omar
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: Sofia
utterances.text: I think maybe the overlap thing is separate from speed, though? Like both can be true.

utterances.speaker: Ravi
utterances.text: They can. I'd want to know whether the thirty-one were the same accounts repeating or thirty-one different ones.

utterances.speaker: Sofia
utterances.text: I don't have that split yet. I can look.

utterances.speaker: Ravi
utterances.text: Do that, and check whether any of the five were on the bigger accounts.

utterances.speaker: Sofia
utterances.text: Okay. I'll try to have it, um, by Friday. Or Monday, maybe.

utterances.speaker: Kofi
utterances.text: Can I ask something? Does the system not have a flag for existing customers?

utterances.speaker: Omar
utterances.text: There's an owner field on the account. The rule just doesn't read it.

utterances.speaker: Kwame
utterances.text: So it could.

utterances.speaker: Omar
utterances.text: Probably. It's more than a checkbox, though. I'd have to look at how it's built.

utterances.speaker: Ravi
utterances.text: Okay. Not today. Let's leave that where it is until we've seen Sofia's breakdown.

utterances.speaker: Omar
utterances.text: Fine by me.

utterances.speaker: Kofi
utterances.text: Yeah, fine.

utterances.speaker: Kwame
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: Ravi
utterances.text: Moving on a bit. Marisol says the queue view is slow in the mornings. Anyone else seeing that?

utterances.speaker: Omar
utterances.text: Mine took like a minute on Tuesday.

utterances.speaker: Sofia
utterances.text: I think maybe mine too? But I was on the train wifi.

utterances.speaker: Ravi
utterances.text: I'll pass it to Sergei. Yara also asked if someone can sit in on the webinar dry run, it's next Tuesday.

utterances.speaker: Omar
utterances.text: What time?

utterances.speaker: Ravi
utterances.text: Two o'clock. Forty-five minutes.

utterances.speaker: Omar
utterances.text: I can do it. Wait, no, that's the one that clashes with the, uh - no, that's Thursday. I can do it.

utterances.speaker: Kofi
utterances.text: Can I raise something else while we're here? It's not about leads.

utterances.speaker: Ravi
utterances.text: Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: Kofi
utterances.text: The pipeline review. I wonder if we should move it off Friday. Wednesday, maybe.

utterances.speaker: Ravi
utterances.text: Why Wednesday in particular?

utterances.speaker: Kofi
utterances.text: It's, um, so if you look at the last fourteen Fridays, nine of them had fewer than four of us in the room.

utterances.speaker: Kofi
utterances.text: And deals slip over the weekend and nobody sees it until Monday, or later.

utterances.speaker: Ravi
utterances.text: Nine of fourteen. I'd have said seven or eight, honestly.

utterances.speaker: Kofi
utterances.text: I counted off the calendar notes. Nine.

utterances.speaker: Sofia
utterances.text: I think maybe Fridays are bad because people take them off? I know I've, um, I've skipped a couple.

utterances.speaker: Omar
utterances.text: I've had customer calls on Friday afternoons pretty much every week.

utterances.speaker: Ravi
utterances.text: Is Wednesday okay for everyone? Kwame?

utterances.speaker: Kwame
utterances.text: Wednesday's fine. I don't have anything standing.

utterances.speaker: Omar
utterances.text: Wednesday morning I have the CRM sync, but that ends at ten.

utterances.speaker: Ravi
utterances.text: Make it eleven, then. All right, Wednesday it is. I'll move the invite after this call and send the new time to everyone.

utterances.speaker: Kofi
utterances.text: Thanks.

utterances.speaker: Sofia
utterances.text: I think maybe I should update my calendar for the first one? Is it this week?

utterances.speaker: Ravi
utterances.text: Next week. This Friday stays as is, since people already planned for it.

utterances.speaker: Sofia
utterances.text: Okay, great.

utterances.speaker: Omar
utterances.text: Does Gabor need to know? He pulls the forecast numbers on Fridays.

utterances.speaker: Ravi
utterances.text: I'll tell him. He can pull them Tuesday night instead.

utterances.speaker: Omar
utterances.text: Got it.

utterances.speaker: Kwame
utterances.text: Back to the double calls for a second. Can I at least see the thirty-one?

utterances.speaker: Sofia
utterances.text: I can send the list, I think maybe tonight? It's in a sheet.

utterances.speaker: Kwame
utterances.text: That'd be good.

utterances.speaker: Ravi
utterances.text: Send it to the group, not just Kwame. I want everyone looking at the same rows.

utterances.speaker: Sofia
utterances.text: Okay, will do.

utterances.speaker: Omar
utterances.text: And I'll check the account owner field, just to see how it's wired. No promises.

utterances.speaker: Ravi
utterances.text: Fine, just look. Nobody changes anything.

utterances.speaker: Omar
utterances.text: Right, just look.

utterances.speaker: Kofi
utterances.text: Are we going to talk about this again next week, or-

utterances.speaker: Ravi
utterances.text: Next week, once we've seen Sofia's numbers. I've got another call, so I need to drop.

utterances.speaker: Omar
utterances.text: Yeah, sounds good.

utterances.speaker: Kwame
utterances.text: Okay. Thanks, Ravi.

utterances.speaker: Ravi
utterances.text: Thanks everyone.

utterances.speaker: Ravi
utterances.text: Okay, I think we're all here. Kwame, can you hear us?

utterances.speaker: Kwame
utterances.text: Yeah, I'm here.

utterances.speaker: Ravi
utterances.text: Good. First, the Wednesday pipeline review. That was the first one. How did it feel?

utterances.speaker: Kofi
utterances.text: Better, I thought. There were, what, five of us?

utterances.speaker: Ravi
utterances.text: Six. Gabor popped in for the forecast bit.

utterances.speaker: Kofi
utterances.text: Six, okay. Still more than most Fridays.

utterances.speaker: Omar
utterances.text: My CRM sync finished at ten so I was fine. Though it did run long, didn't it?

utterances.speaker: Sofia
utterances.text: I think maybe it went past noon? I had to, um, leave for another call.

utterances.speaker: Ravi
utterances.text: Ten past twelve. I'll tighten the agenda next week.

utterances.speaker: Ravi
utterances.text: Next thing, Klara needs the Manchester dinner choices by Friday. If you've got dietary stuff, tell her directly.

utterances.speaker: Omar
utterances.text: There's a place near the station that does a set menu, I could-

utterances.speaker: Ravi
utterances.text: Omar, send it to Klara, not to me.

utterances.speaker: Omar
utterances.text: Yep, will do.

utterances.speaker: Kwame
utterances.text: I'm easy, anything is fine.

utterances.speaker: Ravi
utterances.text: Noted. Yara's webinar dry run was yesterday. Omar, you sat in?

utterances.speaker: Omar
utterances.text: I did. It was fine, the slides are a bit heavy. Forty-five minutes turned into nearly an hour.

utterances.speaker: Kofi
utterances.text: Has the date been locked yet?

utterances.speaker: Ravi
utterances.text: Not yet, Yara's still waiting on one of the speakers.

utterances.speaker: Kofi
utterances.text: Okay, fair enough.

utterances.speaker: Sofia
utterances.text: Um, while we're on admin, the new headset came, finally. No more crackling.

utterances.speaker: Ravi
utterances.text: Good. Okay, the routing rule. We parked it last week and I don't want it sitting any longer. So I'm reopening it now, properly, and we come out of this call with an answer.

utterances.speaker: Omar
utterances.text: Fine by me.

utterances.speaker: Ravi
utterances.text: Sofia, you sent your breakdown on Friday. Walk us through it again, briefly.

utterances.speaker: Sofia
utterances.text: Um, so, I think maybe the main thing is the thirty-one double calls weren't the same few accounts. It was twenty-six different ones.

utterances.speaker: Ravi
utterances.text: Twenty-six accounts. So not one noisy customer.

utterances.speaker: Sofia
utterances.text: Right. And of the five complaints, I think maybe two were on the bigger accounts, the ones that have had a named owner for years.

utterances.speaker: Kwame
utterances.text: Which are the ones we can least afford to annoy.

utterances.speaker: Ravi
utterances.text: Which two?

utterances.speaker: Sofia
utterances.text: I'd have to look up the names. One's in the logistics segment, I know that much.

utterances.speaker: Ravi
utterances.text: Send them round later. Omar, did you look at the owner field?

utterances.speaker: Omar
utterances.text: I did. So it's wired up fine, the owner's right there on the account record. The rule just never reads it. I poked at it in the sandbox, didn't change anything live.

utterances.speaker: Ravi
utterances.text: And?

utterances.speaker: Omar
utterances.text: And it's, uh, not as bad as I thought. The rule has a condition step, I can add one that checks the owner.

utterances.speaker: Kwame
utterances.text: What about when the owner's away?

utterances.speaker: Omar
utterances.text: That's the part I'm still- there's the away toggle again, same one as before. So it could check that.

utterances.speaker: Ravi
utterances.text: Could, or does?

utterances.speaker: Omar
utterances.text: Could. I haven't tried it with an owner who's actually marked away.

utterances.speaker: Ravi
utterances.text: Then I'm not taking that as a given.

utterances.speaker: Omar
utterances.text: No, no, fair.

utterances.speaker: Omar
utterances.text: Can I say the other side though? The plain rotation is simple. Everybody gets the same share, nobody's sitting on a pile. If we start sending things to owners, Vikram's book is huge and he'll get everything.

utterances.speaker: Ravi
utterances.text: Vikram has the biggest book, yes. Roughly a third of the existing accounts, I think.

utterances.speaker: Kwame
utterances.text: Closer to a quarter.

utterances.speaker: Ravi
utterances.text: I'll check the sheet. Say a quarter to a third.

utterances.speaker: Omar
utterances.text: So he gets slammed again, like the old Mondays.

utterances.speaker: Sofia
utterances.text: I think maybe that's only the existing customers though? Not the new ones?

utterances.speaker: Omar
utterances.text: Right, but a hundred twelve out of six-forty, that's still a lot landing on a few people.

utterances.speaker: Ravi
utterances.text: Seventeen percent or so. Not nothing.

utterances.speaker: Kwame
utterances.text: And that's two weeks of it.

utterances.speaker: Kofi
utterances.text: Can I come in here?

utterances.speaker: Ravi
utterances.text: Go ahead, Kofi.

utterances.speaker: Kofi
utterances.text: Okay, so, zooming out. The part that's clearly working is the speed on new stuff, forty minutes versus five hours, we shouldn't touch that. So new accounts keep going round the six of us like now.

utterances.speaker: Kofi
utterances.text: But a customer who already has someone, that one just goes to their person. Straight to them. And if the person's away, it drops back into the rotation, so nobody's left waiting.

utterances.speaker: Kofi
utterances.text: And it's one day of work in the CRM, not a project. So it's cheap for what it fixes.

utterances.speaker: Ravi
utterances.text: A day. Omar, is that realistic?

utterances.speaker: Omar
utterances.text: Um. Yeah, probably. One day including testing, if the away toggle behaves.

utterances.speaker: Ravi
utterances.text: If.

utterances.speaker: Omar
utterances.text: I'd try it first with a dummy owner, like I did with the rotation.

utterances.speaker: Kwame
utterances.text: That's the version I was asking about in the first place.

utterances.speaker: Ravi
utterances.text: You were. Sofia?

utterances.speaker: Sofia
utterances.text: I think maybe it's reasonable? The owner knows the customer, so, um, the second call just goes away.

utterances.speaker: Omar
utterances.text: But Vikram.

utterances.speaker: Kofi
utterances.text: Vikram's customers calling Vikram. That's not a problem, that's his book.

utterances.speaker: Omar
utterances.text: It's the volume I'm thinking about. If he's out a week and it all dumps back into the rotation, fine, but when he's in-

utterances.speaker: Ravi
utterances.text: When he's in, he handles the forms from his own accounts. That's what owning an account means.

utterances.speaker: Omar
utterances.text: Yeah. Okay. I just wanted it said.

utterances.speaker: Ravi
utterances.text: It's said. Kwame, anything?

utterances.speaker: Kwame
utterances.text: No. I'm fine with that. Customers get one call.

utterances.speaker: Ravi
utterances.text: Right. Then here's where I land. New accounts stay in the rotation across all six of you, and any lead from an account that has an owner goes to that owner. Omar, build that.

utterances.speaker: Omar
utterances.text: Okay. When do you want it?

utterances.speaker: Ravi
utterances.text: How soon can you have it?

utterances.speaker: Omar
utterances.text: Thursday, probably. I'll test Wednesday.

utterances.speaker: Ravi
utterances.text: Fine. Early morning flip again, before nine, and you stay on it.

utterances.speaker: Omar
utterances.text: Eight, yeah.

utterances.speaker: Ravi
utterances.text: Marisol needs to know, since the queue will look different to her.

utterances.speaker: Omar
utterances.text: I'll message her today.

utterances.speaker: Kwame
utterances.text: Will she still see all of it?

utterances.speaker: Omar
utterances.text: She will, same as before.

utterances.speaker: Sofia
utterances.text: Should I still send the names of the two complaint accounts?

utterances.speaker: Ravi
utterances.text: Yes, to the group, by tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: Sofia
utterances.text: Okay. I think maybe I'll also add which rep made the second call?

utterances.speaker: Ravi
utterances.text: Useful, yes.

utterances.speaker: Kofi
utterances.text: Should I tell my accounts anything?

utterances.speaker: Ravi
utterances.text: Your accounts' forms will come straight to you now, Kofi. So answer them.

utterances.speaker: Kofi
utterances.text: Oh, right. Yeah, I'll watch my queue.

utterances.speaker: Ravi
utterances.text: I'll write two lines to the group today so everyone knows what changes.

utterances.speaker: Omar
utterances.text: Do you want me to draft it?

utterances.speaker: Ravi
utterances.text: No, I'll do it.

utterances.speaker: Kwame
utterances.text: One thing. I asked Sergei about the laptop refresh.

utterances.speaker: Ravi
utterances.text: And?

utterances.speaker: Kwame
utterances.text: He says November, but not the first batch. Probably us in the second.

utterances.speaker: Ravi
utterances.text: Do we know which week?

utterances.speaker: Kwame
utterances.text: He didn't say. Mid-month maybe.

utterances.speaker: Sofia
utterances.text: I think maybe I should back up my files before? Last time I lost my bookmarks.

utterances.speaker: Omar
utterances.text: There's a sync thing, it should handle most-

utterances.speaker: Ravi
utterances.text: Sergei will send instructions. Don't back anything up yourself yet.

utterances.speaker: Sofia
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: Kofi
utterances.text: Is the offsite still Wednesday to Friday?

utterances.speaker: Ravi
utterances.text: Tuesday to Thursday. Check Klara's email.

utterances.speaker: Kofi
utterances.text: Tuesday. Right, sorry.

utterances.speaker: Omar
utterances.text: Trains to Manchester are cheaper if we book this week, by the way.

utterances.speaker: Ravi
utterances.text: Klara's handling travel. Don't book yourselves.

utterances.speaker: Omar
utterances.text: Oh. Okay, I'll hold off.

utterances.speaker: Sofia
utterances.text: Does she need the dietary stuff today or Friday?

utterances.speaker: Ravi
utterances.text: Friday.

utterances.speaker: Kwame
utterances.text: Mine's already done.

utterances.speaker: Ravi
utterances.text: Good. Anyone else? I need to get to another call.

utterances.speaker: Omar
utterances.text: Nothing from me.

utterances.speaker: Kofi
utterances.text: Nope.

utterances.speaker: Ravi
utterances.text: Thanks all, speak next week.
